This is an analysis task, not a code-change task.

Bottom line: this repo is primarily a live/stored DOS + QuickBASIC data/application snapshot, not a modern layered app. The practical “services” are standalone BASIC programs chained from the main menu. For AMiWinForms parity work, the most important finding is that UI behavior and data access are tightly fused, file schemas are implicit in INPUT#/WRITE# order, and several workflows rely on DOS-era path, printer, locking, and random-file assumptions.

1) What acts as the “application shell”
START.ASC is just a launcher into MAINMENU (CHAIN "MAINMENU"). /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/START.ASC:1-8
MAINM.ASC is the real top-level UI/menu. It reads status/banner files (NOTES-4.ED, CURRENT.DTE, SUBLIMAL.MES), checks workstation date consistency, and dispatches directly to business modules like SHOPCARD, INVOICE, LEDGER, SALES, LOGBOOK, QUOTE, purchase, MESSAGE, VGAFONTS, etc. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/MAINM.ASC:25-36, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/MAINM.ASC:62-87, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/MAINM.ASC:103-151
There is no visible service/repository abstraction. The menu calls modules directly; those modules open files directly.
Why it matters: WinForms parity cannot just “port screens.” It needs an explicit service/data layer extracted from these chained programs.

2) Core data stores and inferred schemas
A. Customer price lists: PRC\<ABBREV>.PRC
PLIST.ASC treats each customer as an 8-char abbreviation mapped to a file PRC\<abbr>.PRC. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PLIST.ASC:20-30
Records are written as:
procedure
effective date
minimum charge
price
unit (/# or /EA)
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PLIST.ASC:141-145
Sample file PRC/ACCESSOR.PRC matches that schema. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PRC/ACCESSOR.PRC:1-58
Why it matters: this is effectively the pricing repository used by invoice generation.

B. Invoice master / A/R index: INVOICE.CHK
This is a random-access binary file, record length 26, with:
9 bytes invoice index
8 bytes amount
8 bytes company code
1 byte status flag
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:92-116, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/ENTIRE.ASC:111-122
Statuses seen in ENTIRE.ASC:
P paid
J unpaid
C amended/corrected cert
V void
E erased
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/ENTIRE.ASC:117-121, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/ENTIRE.ASC:157-163
Maintenance tools INV-FIX.ASC, INVCHK.ASC, LEDGCOPY.ASC exist purely to rebuild/compare this file. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INV-FIX.ASC:6-21, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVCHK.ASC:2-20, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGCOPY.ASC:5-25
Why it matters: INVOICE.CHK appears to be the real unpaid-invoice authority, not just a cache.

C. Sales journal: JOURNAL.CUR
SALES.ASC reads each sales row as:
date
invoice number
PO
amount
customer code
procedure
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/SALES.ASC:29-37
INVOICE_.ASC appends those same 6 fields during invoice update. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:314-320
Sample data matches the 6-field layout. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/JOURNAL.CUR:1-36
Why it matters: this is the sales-history/event log that reporting modules use.

D. Logbook by year: LOGBOOK.yy
LOGBOOK.ASC reads logbook rows as:
date, customer, part number, invoice, PO, spec,
qty accepted, qty rejected, material, heat treat, reason rejected, status
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LOGBOOK.ASC:40-52
LOGENTER.ASC appends that same 12-field structure. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LOGENTER.ASC:30-33
INVOICE_.ASC also appends that same structure during invoice update. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:324-328
Why it matters: this is the inspection/process history the UI uses for traceability and printouts.

E. Cash receipts / check mapping: LEDGER.CUR + CHECK.INV
LEDGER.ASC reads LEDGER.CUR as:
company
date
check number
invoice-difference note
amount
reference
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:60-79
When a check is added, the module:
marks invoice records in INVOICE.CHK paid,
appends check summary to LEDGER.CUR,
appends check-to-invoice linkage to CHECK.INV.
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:163-172
On check deletion, it removes the LEDGER.CUR entry, purges CHECK.INV, and resets invoice flags back to unpaid in INVOICE.CHK. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:197-217, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:405-429
Sample files match this design. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.CUR:1-40, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/CHECK.INV:1-20
Why it matters: A/R status is split across binary invoice master + sequential check journals.

F. Purchasing: VENDOR.DAT, PURCHASE.DAT, ourpo.num
PURCHASE.ASC reads next PO from ourpo.num. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PURCHASE.ASC:16, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PURCHASE.ASC:83-84
It uses VENDOR.DAT as a vendor-name list. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PURCHASE.ASC:49-54, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/VENDOR.DAT:1-40
It writes orders to PURCHASE.DAT as:
vendor, PO#, order date, due date, item, size/unit, qty
part/serial, received, backorder, total cost
/home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PURCHASE.ASC:119-123
Sample purchasing data matches that layout. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PURCHASE.DAT:1-58
Why it matters: another file-backed workflow with no schema outside code.

3) The main business workflows
Invoice creation workflow
INVOICE_.ASC is the most important single file for UI/data coupling:

Loads C.O.D. aging info and non-COD exceptions. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:7-15
Loads standard procedures. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:16-18
Pulls default inspector from INSPECTR.DAT. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:19-21
Requires one or more SHOPCARD\<bucket>\<card>.crd files as source input. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:114-124, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/INVOICE_.ASC:180-191

Check/cash-receipt workflow
LEDGER.ASC validates entered invoice numbers against INVOICE.CHK, prevents duplicates/voids/corrected certs, computes discount/debit notes, and persists both receipt summary and receipt-to-invoice mapping. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:82-173
It also supports non-invoice “other checks” in other.chk. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:247-276, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:303-321
Reporting / admin workflows
SALES.ASC: sales journal lookup, procedure totals, company totals, delete invoice from journal. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/SALES.ASC:14-27, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/SALES.ASC:51-100, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/SALES.ASC:101-121

4) Legacy DOS compatibility assumptions that are everywhere
8-character customer codes are fundamental. Examples: LEFT$(...,8) and *.PRC filename generation in PLIST.ASC, LOGBOOK.ASC, LEDGER.ASC, PURCHASE.ASC. /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PLIST.ASC:20-30, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LOGBOOK.ASC:28-37, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/LEDGER.ASC:85-88, /home/runner/work/AMiDataStore/AMiDataStore/PURCHASE.ASC:45-54

7) Best reconstruction of the data-layer architecture
If I had to describe the effective repository/service model for modernization, it is:

CustomerRepository → REALNAME.DAT, PRC\*.PRC, phone list files
InvoiceRepository → INVOICE.CHK (+ INVOICE.NUM, LASTINVO.ICE, MONTH.INV)
SalesJournalRepository → JOURNAL.CUR
LogbookRepository → LOGBOOK.yy + generated LOGBOOK.BAC
ReceiptRepository → LEDGER.CUR, CHECK.INV, other.chk
PurchasingRepository → VENDOR.DAT, PURCHASE.DAT, ourpo.num
ReferenceDataRepository → PROCDURE.DAT, COD.DAT, COD-NO.DAT, INSPECTR.DAT
8) Most important takeaway for AMiWinForms continuation
The repo does explain the business workflows, but the UI and data layer are not separated at all. For DOS-to-VB parity, the safest path is to treat these files and record layouts as the current contract, especially:

INVOICE.CHK
JOURNAL.CUR
LOGBOOK.yy
CHECK.INV
PRC\*.PRC
The biggest parity risks are:

hidden DOS assumptions (8-char names, drives, printers, SORT/COPY),
stale/duplicate source variants,
binary random-file formats,
missing runtime assets like SHOPCARD,
inconsistent invoice-era logic (e.g. INVOICE_.ASC vs current data volume).
If you want, I can next turn this into a module-by-module modernization map (legacy file → likely WinForms service/model/view) without changing any files.



## Copilot

# 1. Executive Summary

Today’s work was primarily **analysis, reconstruction, and continuity preparation** rather than new coding inside the AMi repositories. The main goal became producing a reliable end-of-day state summary for the AMi modernization effort, with emphasis on **AMiWinForms**, **AMIDataStore**, and **DOS-to-VB parity**. To support that, we also created and pushed this chat history into the dedicated archive repository so the session could be resumed later without losing context.

On the operational side, we successfully:
- cloned `testsubject117/co-pilot-chat-history`,
- copied in the two session files,
- committed them,
- pushed them,
- and verified that the push succeeded even though GitHub reported the repository had moved to the canonical casing `testsubject117/Co-Pilot-Chat-History`.

That archival step matters because today’s AMi work included a lot of **repo investigation and behavior mapping**, and preserving that evidence is important for restart continuity.

On the AMi side, the biggest accomplishment was a **concrete repository-grounded scan of `testsubject117/amiwinforms` and `testsubject117/AMIDataStore`** to recover actual forms, files, workflows, and hidden assumptions rather than guessing. The scan showed that **AMiWinForms already contains a meaningful DOS-style shell and several substantial working workflows**, especially around ledger viewing, check/invoice search, company totals, doesn’t-balance auditing, mileage tracking, and personal calendar behavior. It also showed that the current WinForms app still contains **clear partial areas and navigation gaps**, especially stubbed menu routes, incomplete wiring, and at least one likely broken prompt-to-form handoff.

The **AMiWinForms** findings were especially strong around the app shell and navigation model. Startup is wired to `FormMainMenu`, and the whole menu system is built around a **keyboard-first, DOS-inspired user experience** using `DosMenuFormBase`. That base consolidates ESC handling, command routing, timer/clock behavior, and the black/yellow retro visual style. The main menu and ledger submenu show a deliberate attempt to preserve the old workflow and look-and-feel rather than replacing it with a generic modern desktop UI. That is consistent with the standing project principle: **VB should stay as close to DOS workflow, navigation, and visual familiarity as practical unless deliberately changed**.

At the same time, repo review exposed that this is **not yet a fully finished continuation**. `FormMainMenu` still has multiple options routed to “Not implemented yet.” `FormLedgerMenu` still leaves several actions stubbed, including Add/Delete checks and Add/Delete OTHER checks. There is a particularly important workflow gap in the ledger flow: `OpenViewChecksPromptFlow` in `FormLedgerMenu` prompts for customer/check/year, but the collected values do not appear to be passed into `FormLedgerView`, which instead opens with empty/default filters. That strongly suggests a current mismatch between the DOS prompt flow and the VB implementation.

Another major AMiWinForms finding is that several workflows are **substantial and likely already useful**:
- `FormLedgerView` supports a checks grid plus customer/check/year/month filtering and invoice-side detail loading from `CHECK.INV`.
- `FormLedgerCompanyTotals`, `FormOtherChecksView`, `FormFindByCheckNumber`, `FormFindByInvoiceNumber`, and `FormLedgerDoesntBalance` all appear implemented to varying useful degrees.
- `FormMileageTracking` appears extensive, including CRUD actions, legacy file compatibility, reporting, paged DOS-style viewing, and odometer persistence.
- `FormPersonalCalendar` also appears substantial, with month navigation, scoped search modes, add/delete, lock-based writes, repair tooling, and BASIC-style parsing/writing helpers.

We also learned that **existing code already contains many explicit DOS-compatibility decisions**, not just visual references. Examples include:
- DOS EOF marker handling,
- MBF float decoding,
- random-access `INVOICE.CHK` layout handling,
- `GW-BASIC WRITE#`/CSV-like parsing,
- two-digit year filtering in ledger logic,
- tolerance behavior preserved from DOS in doesn’t-balance logic,
- and DOS indentation semantics in the employee-name editor.

The **AMIDataStore** scan was equally important, but in a different way. It revealed that this repository is **not a modern service/repository layer at all**. It is primarily a **snapshot of DOS/QuickBASIC-era programs plus their live data files**, with the “architecture” embodied in chained BASIC modules and file access patterns. That means UI behavior and persistence logic are tightly coupled in the legacy system. There is no clean abstraction boundary like a typical .NET repository/service model; instead, modules open files directly and rely on field ordering, drive letters, printer devices, shell commands, and DOS naming assumptions.

That AMIDataStore discovery matters because it clarifies what modernization really requires. The WinForms continuation cannot merely redraw screens. It must either:
1. preserve those file layouts and behaviors as a compatibility contract, or
2. deliberately replace them with a modern abstraction while still reproducing DOS business behavior.

The data-store scan identified the major effective data repositories embedded in the DOS app:
- `PRC\*.PRC` as price-list storage,
- `INVOICE.CHK` as a key invoice/A/R index,
- `JOURNAL.CUR` as sales journal history,
- `LOGBOOK.yy` as process/inspection history,
- `LEDGER.CUR` plus `CHECK.INV` as check application / cash receipt storage,
- `VENDOR.DAT`, `PURCHASE.DAT`, and PO-number files for purchasing,
- and reference files like `PROCDURE.DAT`, `COD.DAT`, `COD-NO.DAT`, `INSPECTR.DAT`.

The scan also surfaced important uncertainties and risks:
- some legacy source variants appear duplicated or stale,
- invoice-number limits in `INVOICE_.ASC` do not appear to match current checked-in data,
- some runtime dependencies like `SHOPCARD\...\*.crd` are missing from the repo snapshot,
- and some maintenance utilities exist specifically to reconcile corruption or inconsistencies, which implies fragile historical data relationships.

Overall, today clarified that the project is in a **mixed but promising** state:
- the **WinForms shell and several key workflows exist and are clearly parity-driven**,
- the **legacy data model has now been mapped at a useful level**,
- but **menu integration, workflow completion, and explicit service extraction remain incomplete**,
- and there are still **uncertain areas where the VB implementation may not yet reflect authoritative DOS behavior**.

This means tomorrow’s work can start from a much stronger base: we now know what exists, what appears wired, what is stubbed, what is likely broken, and where the most important DOS contracts live.

## Why those findings matter
These findings matter because they define the real **parity contract** that the WinForms application must either preserve or intentionally replace. The DOS system does not separate UI, business logic, and persistence cleanly. Instead:
- menu modules dispatch directly to business modules,
- business modules manipulate files directly,
- file schemas are implicit in `INPUT#` / `WRITE#` / random-record layouts,
- and data integrity is maintained partly through maintenance utilities and operator workflow rather than robust abstraction layers.

This means AMiWinForms modernization must be careful not to accidentally “modernize away” critical legacy behavior. The safest current interpretation is:
- the data files and layouts are the system of record,
- the DOS workflows define expected behavior,
- and service/repository boundaries in VB need to be derived from those behaviors, not assumed from modern architectural preferences.

# 5. DOS vs VB Parity Summary

## What DOS currently does in the relevant workflow
From the AMIDataStore scan, DOS currently implements:
- a top-level menu-driven application launched via `START.ASC` -> `MAINMENU`
- direct chained transitions into business modules like:
  - ledger,
  - invoice,
  - sales,
  - logbook,
  - purchase,
  - quote,
  - shopcard-related functions
- direct file-backed business workflows without a modern service layer
- invoice creation that:
  - reads COD aging / exemptions,
  - reads standard procedures,
  - reads inspector defaults,
  - consumes `SHOPCARD` card data,
  - resolves real customer names,
  - calculates line amounts,
  - prints to `LPT1:`,
  - updates `JOURNAL.CUR`,
  - updates `LOGBOOK.yy`,
  - updates `INVOICE.CHK`,
  - updates invoice numbering files
- receipt/check application that:
  - validates invoice numbers against `INVOICE.CHK`,
  - prevents invalid or duplicate states,
  - updates `LEDGER.CUR`,
  - updates `CHECK.INV`,
  - toggles paid/unpaid state in `INVOICE.CHK`
- reporting/admin workflows around:
  - sales totals,
  - logbook queries,
  - monthly statements,
  - invoice inquiry,
  - void/erase,
  - backup/rebuild/sort/maintenance utilities

## What VB already reproduces
AMiWinForms already reproduces a meaningful portion of DOS behavior:
- DOS-like startup through a main menu
- keyboard-first navigation
- black/yellow retro menu style
- ESC-driven closing/navigation conventions
- DOS-like menu shell behavior in `DosMenuFormBase`
- ledger/inquiry workflows:
  - view checks
  - company totals
  - other checks
  - find by check number
  - find by invoice number
  - doesn’t-balance audit
- mileage tracking with DOS-style behavior patterns and legacy file compatibility
- personal calendar with keyboard-heavy DOS-style flow and BASIC-like storage helpers
- employee-name editing with preserved DOS indentation semantics
- legacy data parsing behaviors:
  - EOF marker handling
  - MBF decoding
  - WRITE#/CSV-like parsing
  - random-access invoice file layout understanding

## What VB still needs to match
VB still appears to need work in several parity-critical areas:
- live menu routing for operational ledger functions like add/delete checks
- wiring to `FormAddChecks`
- sales employee check generation workflow wiring to `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard`
- correct prompt-to-ledger-view filter transfer
- confirmation that all ledger update behavior truly matches DOS paid/unpaid and check-link semantics
- explicit handling of DOS conventions where not yet surfaced in UI:
  - 8-character customer codes
  - uppercase input behavior
  - device/path semantics
  - any remaining printer/report workflows
- validation/business-rule parity around invoice/check posting, special customer handling, COD behavior, and status transitions

## What visual/behavioral patterns must remain familiar
These patterns should remain familiar unless explicitly changed:
- keyboard-first operation
- visible menu-letter/command patterns
- ESC as a primary exit/back behavior
- DOS-like black background / yellow text where that pattern is still part of the operator mental model
- compact operator-facing workflows rather than wizard-heavy consumer-style UI
- familiar business terms and menu groupings
- ledger/search/reporting navigation that mirrors the DOS sequence
- shortcut-heavy data-entry and inquiry behavior
- legacy tolerance, parsing, and formatting behavior where business meaning depends on it

## Known gaps, mismatches, or deviations
- `FormMainMenu` has visible not-yet-implemented routes
- `FormLedgerMenu` still stubs several operational actions
- `FormAddChecks` exists but appears not reachable from the live ledger menu
- `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard` exists but appears not reachable from the live submenu path
- `OpenViewChecksPromptFlow` likely loses its collected filters before opening `FormLedgerView`
- AMIDataStore shows DOS workflows still tightly coupled to missing runtime assets such as `SHOPCARD`
- some DOS source/data combinations appear stale or inconsistent, meaning “what DOS currently does” may need validation against actual live production behavior, not just checked-in files
- invoice-era/source mismatches in AMIDataStore create uncertainty about which historical source file is authoritative

## Anything explicitly decided can differ
No clear project decision was recorded today stating that a specific behavior should intentionally differ from DOS. The standing principle remains:
- **VB should keep DOS workflow, behavior, navigation, and look-and-feel as closely as practical unless explicitly decided otherwise.**

# 7. Key Technical Findings

- AMiWinForms startup is wired to `FormMainMenu`, confirming the DOS-style menu remains the active shell.
- `DosMenuFormBase.vb` is the key parity infrastructure for:
  - menu behavior,
  - ESC handling,
  - keyboard routing,
  - retro styling,
  - timer/clock behavior.
- The WinForms app is intentionally **keyboard-first**, not just visually retro.
- `FormLedgerMenu` contains both real workflow routes and stubs, making it the clearest “transition zone” between implemented and incomplete functionality.
- `FormLedgerView` appears functionally significant, but the prompt flow likely does not pass collected filters into the form.
- `FormAddChecks.vb` likely represents implemented work that is not yet integrated.
- `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard.vb` likely represents implemented work that is not yet integrated.
- `FormAboutNew.vb` appears to be placeholder/cleanup territory.
- WinForms code already contains explicit DOS-compatibility logic:
  - DOS EOF marker handling (`ChrW(26)`)
  - MBF float decoding
  - GW-BASIC style parser behavior
  - two-digit ledger year filtering
  - DOS tolerance semantics in balancing logic
  - DOS indentation semantics in employee-name editing
- `LegacyDataPaths.vb` and `AppPaths.vb` show continued dependency on legacy UNC paths and network-share assumptions.
- AMIDataStore is not a modern data layer; it is a DOS app/data snapshot whose “services” are BASIC modules chained from menus.
- Legacy data schemas are mostly implicit in file read/write order, not documented in standalone schema definitions.
- `INVOICE.CHK` appears central to invoice status and should be treated as a high-risk parity contract.
- `LEDGER.CUR` and `CHECK.INV` together represent the receipt/check layer.
- `JOURNAL.CUR` and `LOGBOOK.yy` act as critical business-history stores.
- `PRC\*.PRC` plus `REALNAME.DAT` form an effective customer/pricing repository pattern.
- DOS business workflows rely on hidden assumptions:
  - 8-character customer abbreviations
  - uppercase input
  - drive letters
  - printer devices
  - shell utilities
- AMIDataStore contains maintenance/reconciliation utilities (`INV-FIX`, `INVCHK`, `LEDGCOPY`, `LEDGSCAN`, `JOURSCAN`), implying historical corruption or fragility handling is part of system reality.
- `INVOICE_.ASC` appears suspicious/stale relative to current invoice-number data, so not every checked-in BASIC source should automatically be treated as current truth without validation.
- Missing runtime assets like `SHOPCARD\...\*.crd` mean some workflows cannot be fully validated from the repo snapshot alone.
- No README/CI/workflow files were found in the AMiWinForms scan, which means repo-level documentation is weak and continuity must come from code and external notes.

# 11. Risks / Blockers / Open Questions

- **Authoritative legacy truth risk:** some AMIDataStore source files appear inconsistent with current data values, especially invoice numbering.
- **Missing runtime assets:** `SHOPCARD` inputs were referenced in legacy invoice logic but not present in the repo snapshot.
- **Workflow wiring gap:** forms may exist but not be reachable from live menu routes.
- **Behavior drift risk:** if VB wiring is completed without DOS validation, it may look correct but behave differently in subtle operator-important ways.
- **Path coupling risk:** current WinForms and legacy code still depend on network shares / DOS-era path patterns.
- **Data integrity risk:** legacy maintenance utilities imply file corruption/rebuild scenarios are part of normal operational reality.
- **Documentation gap:** absence of README/workflow docs increases dependence on reverse engineering and session continuity notes.
- **Unknown parity status:** no confirmed evidence today that all existing WinForms forms have been operator-tested against DOS outputs.
- **Architecture risk:** introducing too much modern abstraction too early could accidentally sever the exact file-layout semantics the legacy workflows expect.
- **Open question:** Is `FormAddChecks` functionally ready, or does it still depend on additional missing code/services?
- **Open question:** Is `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard` complete enough for immediate wiring, or does it need additional stabilization first?
- **Open question:** Which DOS source files in AMIDataStore reflect the true latest logic versus older exports or variants?
- **Open question:** Should printer-era outputs remain printer-formatted, previewed, exported, or hybrid in the VB continuation?

Because **different tools and repo access paths have different limits**.

### Why it works sometimes and not others
Usually one of these is different:

- **The file is smaller**  
  Small text files often come back with content inline.

- **A different tool is available**  
  Some environments expose a direct file-read tool for GitHub files; this one does not appear to return the full body for these large repo files.

- **The file was provided directly in chat**  
  If you paste content, I can read it immediately.

- **The source is local workspace vs GitHub API metadata**  
  Direct local-file access is different from GitHub contents API access.

- **The platform truncates or suppresses large file bodies**  
  Large blobs often come back as metadata-only or with empty content fields.

- path
- size
- SHA
- html URL

````
# 1. Executive Summary

Today’s work was primarily **analysis, reconstruction, and continuity preparation** rather than new coding inside the AMi repositories. The main goal became producing a reliable end-of-day state summary for the AMi modernization effort, with emphasis on **AMiWinForms**, **AMIDataStore**, and **DOS-to-VB parity**. To support that, we also created and pushed this chat history into the dedicated archive repository so the session could be resumed later without losing context.

On the operational side, we successfully:
- cloned `testsubject117/co-pilot-chat-history`,
- copied in the two session files,
- committed them,
- pushed them,
- and verified that the push succeeded even though GitHub reported the repository had moved to the canonical casing `testsubject117/Co-Pilot-Chat-History`.

That archival step matters because today’s AMi work included a lot of **repo investigation and behavior mapping**, and preserving that evidence is important for restart continuity.

On the AMi side, the biggest accomplishment was a **concrete repository-grounded scan of `testsubject117/amiwinforms` and `testsubject117/AMIDataStore`** to recover actual forms, files, workflows, and hidden assumptions rather than guessing. The scan showed that **AMiWinForms already contains a meaningful DOS-style shell and several substantial working workflows**, especially around ledger viewing, check/invoice search, company totals, doesn’t-balance auditing, mileage tracking, and personal calendar behavior. It also showed that the current WinForms app still contains **clear partial areas and navigation gaps**, especially stubbed menu routes, incomplete wiring, and at least one likely broken prompt-to-form handoff.

The **AMiWinForms** findings were especially strong around the app shell and navigation model. Startup is wired to `FormMainMenu`, and the whole menu system is built around a **keyboard-first, DOS-inspired user experience** using `DosMenuFormBase`. That base consolidates ESC handling, command routing, timer/clock behavior, and the black/yellow retro visual style. The main menu and ledger submenu show a deliberate attempt to preserve the old workflow and look-and-feel rather than replacing it with a generic modern desktop UI. That is consistent with the standing project principle: **VB should stay as close to DOS workflow, navigation, and visual familiarity as practical unless deliberately changed**.

At the same time, repo review exposed that this is **not yet a fully finished continuation**. `FormMainMenu` still has multiple options routed to “Not implemented yet.” `FormLedgerMenu` still leaves several actions stubbed, including Add/Delete checks and Add/Delete OTHER checks. There is a particularly important workflow gap in the ledger flow: `OpenViewChecksPromptFlow` in `FormLedgerMenu` prompts for customer/check/year, but the collected values do not appear to be passed into `FormLedgerView`, which instead opens with empty/default filters. That strongly suggests a current mismatch between the DOS prompt flow and the VB implementation.

Another major AMiWinForms finding is that several workflows are **substantial and likely already useful**:
- `FormLedgerView` supports a checks grid plus customer/check/year/month filtering and invoice-side detail loading from `CHECK.INV`.
- `FormLedgerCompanyTotals`, `FormOtherChecksView`, `FormFindByCheckNumber`, `FormFindByInvoiceNumber`, and `FormLedgerDoesntBalance` all appear implemented to varying useful degrees.
- `FormMileageTracking` appears extensive, including CRUD actions, legacy file compatibility, reporting, paged DOS-style viewing, and odometer persistence.
- `FormPersonalCalendar` also appears substantial, with month navigation, scoped search modes, add/delete, lock-based writes, repair tooling, and BASIC-style parsing/writing helpers.

We also learned that **existing code already contains many explicit DOS-compatibility decisions**, not just visual references. Examples include:
- DOS EOF marker handling,
- MBF float decoding,
- random-access `INVOICE.CHK` layout handling,
- `GW-BASIC WRITE#`/CSV-like parsing,
- two-digit year filtering in ledger logic,
- tolerance behavior preserved from DOS in doesn’t-balance logic,
- and DOS indentation semantics in the employee-name editor.

The **AMIDataStore** scan was equally important, but in a different way. It revealed that this repository is **not a modern service/repository layer at all**. It is primarily a **snapshot of DOS/QuickBASIC-era programs plus their live data files**, with the “architecture” embodied in chained BASIC modules and file access patterns. That means UI behavior and persistence logic are tightly coupled in the legacy system. There is no clean abstraction boundary like a typical .NET repository/service model; instead, modules open files directly and rely on field ordering, drive letters, printer devices, shell commands, and DOS naming assumptions.

That AMIDataStore discovery matters because it clarifies what modernization really requires. The WinForms continuation cannot merely redraw screens. It must either:
1. preserve those file layouts and behaviors as a compatibility contract, or
2. deliberately replace them with a modern abstraction while still reproducing DOS business behavior.

The data-store scan identified the major effective data repositories embedded in the DOS app:
- `PRC\*.PRC` as price-list storage,
- `INVOICE.CHK` as a key invoice/A/R index,
- `JOURNAL.CUR` as sales journal history,
- `LOGBOOK.yy` as process/inspection history,
- `LEDGER.CUR` plus `CHECK.INV` as check application / cash receipt storage,
- `VENDOR.DAT`, `PURCHASE.DAT`, and PO-number files for purchasing,
- and reference files like `PROCDURE.DAT`, `COD.DAT`, `COD-NO.DAT`, `INSPECTR.DAT`.

The scan also surfaced important uncertainties and risks:
- some legacy source variants appear duplicated or stale,
- invoice-number limits in `INVOICE_.ASC` do not appear to match current checked-in data,
- some runtime dependencies like `SHOPCARD\...\*.crd` are missing from the repo snapshot,
- and some maintenance utilities exist specifically to reconcile corruption or inconsistencies, which implies fragile historical data relationships.

Overall, today clarified that the project is in a **mixed but promising** state:
- the **WinForms shell and several key workflows exist and are clearly parity-driven**,
- the **legacy data model has now been mapped at a useful level**,
- but **menu integration, workflow completion, and explicit service extraction remain incomplete**,
- and there are still **uncertain areas where the VB implementation may not yet reflect authoritative DOS behavior**.

This means tomorrow’s work can start from a much stronger base: we now know what exists, what appears wired, what is stubbed, what is likely broken, and where the most important DOS contracts live.

# 4. AMiDataStore Work Summary

## Data access behavior reviewed
AMIDataStore was confirmed to be primarily a **legacy DOS/QuickBASIC application/data snapshot**, not a modern C#/VB data-access library. Data access behavior is embodied in BASIC modules that directly open and manipulate flat files, random-access files, and supporting data files.

Key legacy stores and their observed roles:

- `PRC\*.PRC`
  - customer pricing records
  - implicitly structured by write order
- `INVOICE.CHK`
  - random-access invoice/A/R index
  - appears central to paid/unpaid state
- `JOURNAL.CUR`
  - sales journal / invoice history
- `LOGBOOK.yy`
  - traceability/process/inspection history by year
- `LEDGER.CUR`
  - check summary / receipt entries
- `CHECK.INV`
  - check-to-invoice mapping
- `other.chk`
  - non-invoice other checks workflow
- `VENDOR.DAT`
  - vendor-name list
- `PURCHASE.DAT`
  - purchasing/order history
- `ourpo.num`
  - next PO source
- `REALNAME.DAT`
  - customer full-name mapping
- `PROCDURE.DAT`
  - procedures reference
- `COD.DAT` / `COD-NO.DAT`
  - COD aging / exception handling
- `INSPECTR.DAT` / `INSPECT.DAT`
  - inspector/default inspector reference
- `INVOICE.NUM`
  - current/next invoice numbering
- `LASTINVO.ICE`
  - last invoice number
- `MONTH.INV`
  - month-to-invoice mapping role

## Dependencies identified
The scan found pervasive dependencies on:
- DOS path conventions
- drive letters (`A:`, `C:`, `F:`)
- direct file access with no abstraction
- random-access file layout assumptions
- printer devices (`LPT1:`, `LPRINT`)
- shell commands/utilities:
  - `SORT`
  - `COPY`
  - `ZIP`
  - `UNZIP`
  - `BIGSORT`
  - `PRINT`
  - `TYPE`
- uppercase input assumptions / Caps Lock style entry
- 8-character customer abbreviations
- external/runtime file availability such as `SHOPCARD\...\*.crd`

## Repository interactions
Reviewed BASIC/source/data files included:
- `START.ASC`
- `MAINM.ASC`
- `LEDGER.ASC`
- `LOGBOOK.ASC`
- `PURCHASE.ASC`

## Why those findings matter
These findings matter because they define the real **parity contract** that the WinForms application must either preserve or intentionally replace. The DOS system does not separate UI, business logic, and persistence cleanly. Instead:
- menu modules dispatch directly to business modules,
- business modules manipulate files directly,
- file schemas are implicit in `INPUT#` / `WRITE#` / random-record layouts,
- and data integrity is maintained partly through maintenance utilities and operator workflow rather than robust abstraction layers.

This means AMiWinForms modernization must be careful not to accidentally “modernize away” critical legacy behavior. The safest current interpretation is:
- the data files and layouts are the system of record,
- the DOS workflows define expected behavior,
- and service/repository boundaries in VB need to be derived from those behaviors, not assumed from modern architectural preferences.

# 5. DOS vs VB Parity Summary

## What DOS currently does in the relevant workflow
From the AMIDataStore scan, DOS currently implements:
- a top-level menu-driven application launched via `START.ASC` -> `MAINMENU`
- direct chained transitions into business modules like:
  - ledger,
  - invoice,
  - sales,
  - logbook,
  - purchase,
  - quote,
  - shopcard-related functions
- direct file-backed business workflows without a modern service layer
- invoice creation that:
  - reads COD aging / exemptions,
  - reads standard procedures,
  - reads inspector defaults,
  - consumes `SHOPCARD` card data,
  - resolves real customer names,
  - calculates line amounts,
  - prints to `LPT1:`,
  - updates `JOURNAL.CUR`,
  - updates `LOGBOOK.yy`,
  - updates `INVOICE.CHK`,
  - updates invoice numbering files
- receipt/check application that:
  - validates invoice numbers against `INVOICE.CHK`,
  - prevents invalid or duplicate states,
  - updates `LEDGER.CUR`,
  - updates `CHECK.INV`,
  - toggles paid/unpaid state in `INVOICE.CHK`
- reporting/admin workflows around:
  - sales totals,
  - logbook queries,
  - monthly statements,
  - invoice inquiry,
  - void/erase,
  - backup/rebuild/sort/maintenance utilities

## What VB already reproduces
AMiWinForms already reproduces a meaningful portion of DOS behavior:
- DOS-like startup through a main menu
- keyboard-first navigation
- black/yellow retro menu style
- ESC-driven closing/navigation conventions
- DOS-like menu shell behavior in `DosMenuFormBase`
- ledger/inquiry workflows:
  - view checks
  - company totals
  - other checks
  - find by check number
  - find by invoice number
  - doesn’t-balance audit
- mileage tracking with DOS-style behavior patterns and legacy file compatibility
- personal calendar with keyboard-heavy DOS-style flow and BASIC-like storage helpers
- employee-name editing with preserved DOS indentation semantics
- legacy data parsing behaviors:
  - EOF marker handling
  - MBF decoding
  - WRITE#/CSV-like parsing
  - random-access invoice file layout understanding

## What VB still needs to match
VB still appears to need work in several parity-critical areas:
- live menu routing for operational ledger functions like add/delete checks
- wiring to `FormAddChecks`
- sales employee check generation workflow wiring to `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard`
- correct prompt-to-ledger-view filter transfer
- confirmation that all ledger update behavior truly matches DOS paid/unpaid and check-link semantics
- explicit handling of DOS conventions where not yet surfaced in UI:
  - 8-character customer codes
  - uppercase input behavior
  - device/path semantics
  - any remaining printer/report workflows
- validation/business-rule parity around invoice/check posting, special customer handling, COD behavior, and status transitions

## What visual/behavioral patterns must remain familiar
These patterns should remain familiar unless explicitly changed:
- keyboard-first operation
- visible menu-letter/command patterns
- ESC as a primary exit/back behavior
- DOS-like black background / yellow text where that pattern is still part of the operator mental model
- compact operator-facing workflows rather than wizard-heavy consumer-style UI
- familiar business terms and menu groupings
- ledger/search/reporting navigation that mirrors the DOS sequence
- shortcut-heavy data-entry and inquiry behavior
- legacy tolerance, parsing, and formatting behavior where business meaning depends on it

## Known gaps, mismatches, or deviations
- `FormMainMenu` has visible not-yet-implemented routes
- `FormLedgerMenu` still stubs several operational actions
- `FormAddChecks` exists but appears not reachable from the live ledger menu
- `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard` exists but appears not reachable from the live submenu path
- `OpenViewChecksPromptFlow` likely loses its collected filters before opening `FormLedgerView`
- AMIDataStore shows DOS workflows still tightly coupled to missing runtime assets such as `SHOPCARD`
- some DOS source/data combinations appear stale or inconsistent, meaning “what DOS currently does” may need validation against actual live production behavior, not just checked-in files
- invoice-era/source mismatches in AMIDataStore create uncertainty about which historical source file is authoritative

## Anything explicitly decided can differ
No clear project decision was recorded today stating that a specific behavior should intentionally differ from DOS. The standing principle remains:
- **VB should keep DOS workflow, behavior, navigation, and look-and-feel as closely as practical unless explicitly decided otherwise.**

# 7. Key Technical Findings

- AMiWinForms startup is wired to `FormMainMenu`, confirming the DOS-style menu remains the active shell.
- `DosMenuFormBase.vb` is the key parity infrastructure for:
  - menu behavior,
  - ESC handling,
  - keyboard routing,
  - retro styling,
  - timer/clock behavior.
- The WinForms app is intentionally **keyboard-first**, not just visually retro.
- `FormLedgerMenu` contains both real workflow routes and stubs, making it the clearest “transition zone” between implemented and incomplete functionality.
- `FormLedgerView` appears functionally significant, but the prompt flow likely does not pass collected filters into the form.
- `FormAddChecks.vb` likely represents implemented work that is not yet integrated.
- `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard.vb` likely represents implemented work that is not yet integrated.
- `FormAboutNew.vb` appears to be placeholder/cleanup territory.
- WinForms code already contains explicit DOS-compatibility logic:
  - DOS EOF marker handling (`ChrW(26)`)
  - MBF float decoding
  - GW-BASIC style parser behavior
  - two-digit ledger year filtering
  - DOS tolerance semantics in balancing logic
  - DOS indentation semantics in employee-name editing
- `LegacyDataPaths.vb` and `AppPaths.vb` show continued dependency on legacy UNC paths and network-share assumptions.
- AMIDataStore is not a modern data layer; it is a DOS app/data snapshot whose “services” are BASIC modules chained from menus.
- Legacy data schemas are mostly implicit in file read/write order, not documented in standalone schema definitions.
- `INVOICE.CHK` appears central to invoice status and should be treated as a high-risk parity contract.
- `LEDGER.CUR` and `CHECK.INV` together represent the receipt/check layer.
- `JOURNAL.CUR` and `LOGBOOK.yy` act as critical business-history stores.
- `PRC\*.PRC` plus `REALNAME.DAT` form an effective customer/pricing repository pattern.
- DOS business workflows rely on hidden assumptions:
  - 8-character customer abbreviations
  - uppercase input
  - drive letters
  - printer devices
  - shell utilities
- AMIDataStore contains maintenance/reconciliation utilities (`INV-FIX`, `INVCHK`, `LEDGCOPY`, `LEDGSCAN`, `JOURSCAN`), implying historical corruption or fragility handling is part of system reality.
- `INVOICE_.ASC` appears suspicious/stale relative to current invoice-number data, so not every checked-in BASIC source should automatically be treated as current truth without validation.
- Missing runtime assets like `SHOPCARD\...\*.crd` mean some workflows cannot be fully validated from the repo snapshot alone.
- No README/CI/workflow files were found in the AMiWinForms scan, which means repo-level documentation is weak and continuity must come from code and external notes.

# 11. Risks / Blockers / Open Questions

- **Authoritative legacy truth risk:** some AMIDataStore source files appear inconsistent with current data values, especially invoice numbering.
- **Missing runtime assets:** `SHOPCARD` inputs were referenced in legacy invoice logic but not present in the repo snapshot.
- **Workflow wiring gap:** forms may exist but not be reachable from live menu routes.
- **Behavior drift risk:** if VB wiring is completed without DOS validation, it may look correct but behave differently in subtle operator-important ways.
- **Path coupling risk:** current WinForms and legacy code still depend on network shares / DOS-era path patterns.
- **Data integrity risk:** legacy maintenance utilities imply file corruption/rebuild scenarios are part of normal operational reality.
- **Documentation gap:** absence of README/workflow docs increases dependence on reverse engineering and session continuity notes.
- **Unknown parity status:** no confirmed evidence today that all existing WinForms forms have been operator-tested against DOS outputs.
- **Architecture risk:** introducing too much modern abstraction too early could accidentally sever the exact file-layout semantics the legacy workflows expect.
- **Open question:** Is `FormAddChecks` functionally ready, or does it still depend on additional missing code/services?
- **Open question:** Is `FormSalesEmployeeCheckWizard` complete enough for immediate wiring, or does it need additional stabilization first?
- **Open question:** Which DOS source files in AMIDataStore reflect the true latest logic versus older exports or variants?
- **Open question:** Should printer-era outputs remain printer-formatted, previewed, exported, or hybrid in the VB continuation?
````

## @testsubject117

I have another question. is there a utility I could use to split the .md file into several smaller .txt files?

## Copilot

Yes — easiest options are **PowerShell** or a generic file-splitter utility. Since you’re already in PowerShell on Windows, that’s probably the best answer.

## Split a large `.md` into smaller `.txt` chunks by line count

This creates numbered text files of 2,000 lines each:

```powershell
$source = "H:\AM\Backed up CoPilot Sessions\tue_may_19_2026_preparing_for_a_break_in_work.md"
$outDir = "H:\AM\Backed up CoPilot Sessions\split"

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outDir | Out-Null

$chunkSize = 2000
$i = 0
$chunk = @()

Get-Content $source | ForEach-Object {
    $chunk += $_
    if ($chunk.Count -ge $chunkSize) {
        $file = Join-Path $outDir ("tue_may_19_2026_preparing_for_a_break_in_work_part_{0:D3}.txt" -f $i)
        $chunk | Set-Content $file
        $i++
        $chunk = @()
    }
}

if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
    $file = Join-Path $outDir ("tue_may_19_2026_preparing_for_a_break_in_work_part_{0:D3}.txt" -f $i)
    $chunk | Set-Content $file
}
```

## Split by approximate file size instead of line count
If you want, I can give you a byte-size-based splitter too, but **line-count splitting is usually safer** for markdown/text.

## Faster one-liner style using batches
If you just want something shorter:

```powershell
$source = "H:\AM\Backed up CoPilot Sessions\tue_may_19_2026_preparing_for_a_break_in_work.md"
$outDir = "H:\AM\Backed up CoPilot Sessions\split"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outDir | Out-Null
$lines = Get-Content $source
0..([math]::Floor(($lines.Count-1)/2000)) | ForEach-Object {
    $start = $_ * 2000
    $end = [math]::Min($start + 1999, $lines.Count - 1)
    $lines[$start..$end] | Set-Content (Join-Path $outDir ("part_{0:D3}.txt" -f $_))
}
```

## If you want a GUI utility
Yes, there are file-splitting utilities, but for plain text/markdown, PowerShell is usually better because:
- no install needed,
- reproducible,
- easy to control line counts,
- preserves text readability.

## Practical recommendation
If your goal is for me to ingest the contents in manageable pieces, I’d suggest:
- split into **1000–3000 line chunks**
- name them sequentially
- optionally also create a **summary/reload-pack file** as chunk 000

If you want, I can give you a version that:

2. names the chunks cleanly,

```powershell
        $file = Join-Path $outDir ("tue_may_19_2026_preparing_for_a_break_in_work_part_{0:D3}.txt" -f $i)
        $chunk | Set-Content $file
        $i++
        $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    }
}

if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
    $file = Join-Path $outDir ("tue_may_19_2026_preparing_for_a_break_in_work_part_{0:D3}.txt" -f $i)
    $chunk | Set-Content $file
}
```

# Option C: One reusable script you can run daily

Save this as:

```text
C:\Users\capnkirk\source\repos\AmiWinForms\co-pilot-chat-history\Split-ChatHistory.ps1
```

```powershell
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [string]$SourceFile,

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [string]$RepoPath,

    [int]$ChunkSize = 2000
)

$baseName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($SourceFile)
$outDir = Join-Path $RepoPath ($baseName + "_parts")

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outDir | Out-Null

$i = 1
$chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]

Get-Content $SourceFile | ForEach-Object {
    $chunk.Add($_)
    if ($chunk.Count -ge $ChunkSize) {
        $file = Join-Path $outDir ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $i)
        $chunk | Set-Content $file
        $i++
        $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    }
}

if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
    $file = Join-Path $outDir ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $i)
    $chunk | Set-Content $file
}

Write-Host "Created split files in: $outDir"
Get-ChildItem $outDir | Select-Object Name, Length
```

```powershell
  -RepoPath "C:\Users\capnkirk\source\repos\AmiWinForms\co-pilot-chat-history"
```

Here’s the architecture I’d carry forward for a faithful WinForms continuation.

1) Top-level runtime shape
Boot/login is DOS + mapped drive oriented. AUTOEXEC.BAT loads SHARE, sets up LAN tooling, then calls LOGIN.BAT; LOGIN.BAT switches to F: and starts gwbasic mainmenu (AUTOEXEC.BAT:1-35, LOGIN.BAT:1-7).
The readable main menu source is effectively in START.ASC, even though it saves/targets MAINMENU; it is the hub that launches almost every business module (START.ASC:5-18, START.ASC:62-88, START.ASC:104-151).
Main menu options dispatch to:
shop cards (SHOPCARD)
invoice generation (INVOICE)
customer payments / receipts (LEDGER)
sales journal (SALES)
logbook (LOGBOOK)
pricing (PLIST)
A/R inquiry (ENTIRE)
purchasing (PURCHASE)
cash disbursements / deposits / vendors (BILL)
admin/update utilities (BOOT) (START.ASC:104-151).
2) Core business data model
There are really three ledgers:

Operational production history

LOGBOOK.yy: one record per invoiced part/line, including customer, part, invoice, PO, spec string, qty accepted/rejected, material, heat treat, reject reason, status (INVOICE_.ASC:325-327, LOGBOOK.ASC:42-47).
Current samples match that schema (LOGBOOK.25:1-12, LOGBOOK.26:1-12).
Sales journal

JOURNAL.CUR: one record per invoiced procedure/charge line: date, invoice, PO, amount, customer code, procedure (INVOICE_.ASC:314-320).
Current samples match that 6-field sequential schema (JOURNAL.CUR:1-12).
Accounts receivable status

INVOICE.CHK: random-access invoice master keyed by invoice - 75000, storing invoice slot, amount due, customer code, and 1-char status (INVOICE_.ASC:344-356, ENTIRE.ASC:111-122).
Status semantics are:
J = unpaid/open
P = paid by customer check
C = corrected cert
V = void
E = erased/administratively removed (ENTIRE.ASC:117-121, ENTIRE.ASC:158-162, ENTIRE.ASC:257-260).
That split is central: invoices are printed from shopcards + price lists, then persisted into all three stores.

3) Main workflows
A. Shopcard creation
Shopcards are created per customer abbreviation, which must correspond to a PRC\<abbr>.PRC price-list file (SHOP.BAS:19-40, PLIST.ASC:18-30).
Shopcards are stored under a bucketed path SHOPCARD\<INT(card/200)>\<card>.CRD (INVOICE_.ASC:124, SHOP-OLD.BAS:571-580).
Stored header fields are:
customer code
part number
PO
heat treat
material
pan count
box count
weight
qty accepted/received proxy
quantity received
followed by repeated (section, field, value) triples for populated attributes (SHOP-OLD.BAS:573-579).
B. Invoice generation
Invoice entry begins by choosing 1–6 shopcards and validating same customer / PO family (INVOICE_.ASC:110-151, INVOICE_.ASC:180-188).
The customer’s price list is PRC\<abbr>.PRC; each record is procedure-part, effective date, minimum charge, price, /EA or /# (PLIST.ASC:143-145, PRC/3VFASTEN.PRC:1-12, PRC/PACIFICC.PRC:1-30).
The invoice module loads:
COD.DAT for delinquent COD warnings (INVOICE_.ASC:7-12, COD.DAT:1-21)
COD-NO.DAT for exemptions (INVOICE_.ASC:13-15, COD-NO.DAT:1-8)
PROCDURE.DAT for the canonical procedure vocabulary (INVOICE_.ASC:16-18, PROCDURE.DAT:1-40)
INSPECTR.DAT for default inspector name (INVOICE_.ASC:20, INVOICE_.ASC:224-225, INVOICE_.ASC:545-557).
It calculates charges from the selected procedures and shopcard quantities/weights, applying minimum charges and special test logic for salt spray / humidity / copper sulfate (INVOICE_.ASC:35-74).
It resolves the customer’s actual printable name from REALNAME.DAT (INVOICE_.ASC:192-200, REALNAME.DAT:1-40).
Special customer workflows exist for PACIFICC and WESTERNC, including custom line packing and engine-model / serial prompts (INVOICE_.ASC:271-272, INVOICE_.ASC:323-328, INVOICE_.ASC:714-781, PRC/PACIFICC.PRC:1-30, PRC/WESTERNC.PRC:1-30, WESTERNC.MAG:1-40).
FAA stamp defaults on for a hardcoded customer set and can be toggled (INVOICE_.ASC:185-186, INVOICE_.ASC:222-234, INVOICE_.ASC:371-380).
C. Printing and updating invoice records
Printing writes directly to LPT1: and uses LPRINT escape sequences; this is not abstracted (INVOICE_.ASC:367-416).
After printing, or via “update without print,” it:
appends procedure lines to JOURNAL.CUR (INVOICE_.ASC:314-320)
appends part-level entries to LOGBOOK.yy (INVOICE_.ASC:323-328)
updates invoice month markers / last invoice trackers (INVOICE_.ASC:330-335)
updates INVOICE.CHK random-access state (INVOICE_.ASC:344-356)
updates INVOICE.NUM to the last used invoice number (INVOICE_.ASC:363-365).
D. Customer check / receipt posting
LEDGER.ASC is really the customer receipts module, not the invoice ledger.
When entering a customer check, it validates each invoice number against INVOICE.CHK, rejects already paid / corrected / void invoices, and then flips those invoice flags to P (LEDGER.ASC:83-118, LEDGER.ASC:163-172).
It appends:
a summary record to LEDGER.CUR
a header + invoice-number list to CHECK.INV (LEDGER.ASC:167-172).
CHECK.INV format is:
customer, check#, reference, date, amount, count, then count invoice numbers (LEDGER.ASC:169-171, CHECK.INV:1-18).
LEDGER.CUR current live format is six sequential fields: customer, date, check#, difference-text, amount, reference (LEDGER.ASC:60-79, LEDGER.CUR:1-12).
E. A/R inquiry / unpaid management
ENTIRE.ASC is the A/R inquiry and maintenance console over INVOICE.CHK:
view one invoice
scan invoice ranges
print invoice ranges
unpaid views
monthly statements
mark invoices paid
edit flags / amount / customer name
COD editor handoff (ENTIRE.ASC:56-103, ENTIRE.ASC:111-180, ENTIRE.ASC:255-266, ENTIRE.ASC:721-722).
It relies almost entirely on INVOICE.CHK; it is not reconstructing from JOURNAL.CUR.
F. Sales and logbook analysis
SALES.ASC reads JOURNAL.CUR for customer history, invoice lookup, procedure totals, and deletion of sales-journal entries (SALES.ASC:14-27, SALES.ASC:29-49, SALES.ASC:62-99, SALES.ASC:101-121).
LOGBOOK.ASC reads LOGBOOK.yy for customer/PO/invoice lookup, “last date of business,” spec scanning across years, and error scans (LOGBOOK.ASC:21-38, LOGBOOK.ASC:40-60, LOGBOOK.ASC:62-105, LOGBOOK.ASC:106-116).
G. Purchasing
PURCHASE.ASC is a separate purchasing subsystem.
Vendor names are selected from VENDOR.DAT; purchase orders are stored in PURCHASE.DAT; next internal PO number is in OURPO.NUM (PURCHASE.ASC:16, PURCHASE.ASC:45-55, PURCHASE.ASC:74-83, PURCHASE.ASC:118-123; VENDOR.DAT:1-40, PURCHASE.DAT:1-40).
PURCHASE.DAT is sequential 2-line-per-order:
line 1: vendor, PO#, order date, due date, description, misc/unit, qty
line 2: part/serial, received flag/text, backorder text, total cost (PURCHASE.ASC:118-123, PURCHASE.ASC:136-153).
H. Cash disbursements / deposits / payroll-like payments
BILL.BAS handles vendor checks, deposits, payroll entries, voids, vendor master maintenance, and cash-disbursement reporting (BILL.BAS:43-54, BILL.BAS:151-176, BILL.BAS:437-451).
Key files:
CHECKNO.DAT = last check number (BILL.BAS:41, BILL.BAS:150)
BILLS.DAT = sequential check register (BILL.BAS:243, BILL.BAS:342-402)
DEPCHECK.DAT = running not-yet-deposited amount (BILL.BAS:248-250, BILL.BAS:280-301)
PAYDEP.DAT = deposits + payroll/deposit events (BILL.BAS:298-301, BILL.BAS:325, BILL.BAS:408-434)
BILLSCHK.DAT = random-access cash/uncashed flags per check (BILL.BAS:252-259, BILL.BAS:456-464, BILL.BAS:724-731, BILL.BAS:755-768).
4) File contracts / implicit schemas
PRC\*.PRC
Sequential text records: procedure, effective date, minimum charge, price, unit (PLIST.ASC:143-145).
Customer abbreviation is the filename stem and is normally 1–8 uppercase chars, no spaces or periods (PLIST.ASC:18-30).
REALNAME.DAT
Alternating pairs: <abbr>.PRC, actual long customer name (PLIST.ASC:241-243, INVOICE_.ASC:192-199, REALNAME.DAT:1-40).
PROCDURE.DAT
One standard procedure token per line; both pricing and invoicing use it to validate/extend vocabulary (PLIST.ASC:11-13, PLIST.ASC:113-132, INVOICE_.ASC:16-18, INVOICE_.ASC:629-647, PROCDURE.DAT:1-40).
COD.DAT
First line is a date; subsequent rows are customer, oldest-date, days, amount (INVOICE_.ASC:7-12, COD.DAT:1-21).
COD-NO.DAT
One exempt customer code per line (INVOICE_.ASC:13-15, COD.ASC:14-18, COD-NO.DAT:1-8).
INVOICE.NUM
Single numeric last invoice used; next invoice is +1 (INVOICE_.ASC:95-96, INVOICE_.ASC:152-155, INVOICE.NUM:1).
LASTINVO.ICE
Last invoice number and date; used with MONTH.INV to track month boundaries (INVOICE_.ASC:330-335, LASTINVO.ICE:1).
MONTH.INV
Month boundary lookup for statements/history, but there is a schema mismatch:
invoice writer updates only 80 entries (INVOICE_.ASC:331-334)
ENTIRE.ASC reads 399 entries (ENTIRE.ASC:40-41).
INVOICE.CHK
Random-access, 26 bytes/record:
9-byte invoice slot (MKS$)
8-byte amount (MKS$)
8-byte customer code
1-byte status (INVOICE_.ASC:163-167, INVOICE_.ASC:344-356).
CHECK.INV
Sequential receipt-to-invoice bridge (LEDGER.ASC:169-171, CHECK.INV:1-18).
LEDGER.CUR
Current live file appears to hold only customer check receipts, not invoice debits (LEDGER.ASC:60-79, LEDGER.CUR:1-12).
JOURNAL.CUR
Sequential sales lines (INVOICE_.ASC:314-320, JOURNAL.CUR:1-12).
LOGBOOK.yy
Sequential operational records keyed by invoice line, stored per 2-digit year suffix (INVOICE_.ASC:324-327, LOGBOOK.ASC:3-8, LOGBOOK.26:1-12).
5) Hidden assumptions you’ll need to preserve
Uppercase operator input is expected everywhere. Many modules explicitly reject lowercase and tell the user to hit Caps Lock (START.ASC:103, LEDGER.ASC:52-59, LOGBOOK.ASC:39, PLIST.ASC:22-27, SHOP.BAS:27-37).
Customer IDs are 8-char uppercase abbreviations and drive filenames (PRC\<abbr>.PRC) and invoice/customer joins (PLIST.ASC:18-30, LEDGER.ASC:52-59, LOGBOOK.ASC:28-29, REALNAME.DAT:1-40).
Path conventions matter. The app assumes a DOS root plus mapped F: and many relative working directories (LOGIN.BAT:1-7, START.ASC:129-147, PHONE.ASC:92-106, PHONE.ASC:120-152).
Device/printer assumptions are hardcoded.
invoices print to LPT1: (INVOICE_.ASC:367-416)
many reports use LPRINT directly (SALES.ASC:79-99, BOOT.ASC:93-100, BILL.BAS:546-567)
printer readiness is polled through DOS errors 24/25/27/57/68 in nearly every module (START.ASC:46-47, INVOICE_.ASC:24-25, LEDGER.ASC:9-10).
Random-access binary encoding uses GW/QB numeric packing (MKS$, CVS) and slot math, so WinForms continuation must preserve exact semantics if it reads existing files (INVOICE_.ASC:163-167, INVOICE_.ASC:344-356, BILL.BAS:252-259, BILL.BAS:724-731).
File locking / single-user contention is part of normal behavior via LOCK, SHARED, and “someone is using your file” retry loops (START.ASC:46, INVOICE_.ASC:24, LEDGER.ASC:9, PLIST.ASC:206-212).
6) Stale/duplicate source variants and inconsistencies
This repo has multiple generations of the same app:

Menu logic is readable in START.ASC, while MAINMENU.BAS in this clone is not useful as source; naming is already split (START.ASC:5-18).
Invoice has many variants: INVOICE.BAS, INVOICE0.BAS, INVOICE1.BAS, INVOICE2.BAS, INVOICE-.BAS, INVOICE_.BAS, INVOICEE.BAS, plus INVCOPY.BAS.
The readable older invoice source (INVOICE_.ASC) differs materially from INVCOPY.BAS; the newer branch adds Lexmark handling, cad-plating fields, more spec items, and changed standards (INVOICE_.ASC:75-81, INVCOPY.BAS:5-9, INVCOPY.BAS:104-112).
Shopcard writer and invoice reader are not perfectly aligned in the readable sources:
shopcard writer can append -1,-1,SER$ sentinel triples (SHOP-OLD.BAS:580)
INVOICE_.ASC shopcard reader blindly assigns every remaining triple into A$(CT,X,Y) with no sentinel handling (INVOICE_.ASC:180-191).
That strongly suggests the active runtime likely used a different invoice branch than INVOICE_.ASC, or that serial support was only partially merged.
Ledger file expectations are inconsistent:
LEDGER.ASC current UI reads 6-field receipt summaries (LEDGER.ASC:60-79)
BOOT.ASC invoice-void/update code still expects mixed "+" debit / "-" credit records (BOOT.ASC:187-201)
CONVTLED.ASC exists specifically to strip the old signed format down to the current check-only format (CONVTLED.ASC:1-8).
MONTH.INV size disagreement (80 vs 399 slots) is another strong sign of drift between invoice and inquiry branches (INVOICE_.ASC:331-334, ENTIRE.ASC:40-41).
7) Missing runtime assets / dangling dependencies
I found clear dangling references:

Main menu option W chains PHMESAGE, but no PHMESAGE* file exists in the repo (START.ASC:141).
Main menu backup path chains BAKFILES.BAS, but no BAKFILES* file exists (START.ASC:163).
I also found environment-state files that code expects but this repo does not contain:

C:\PMS.ED (START.ASC:199)
C:\PAYROLL.CHK (START.ASC:216)
C:\CDRIVE.CHK (START.ASC:221)
BKUP.DTE (START.ASC:153)
C:\LASER.CHK / C:\LEXMARK.CHK printer markers (SHOP.BAS:6-7, INVCOPY.BAS:5).
Those look intentional/environmental, but they matter because behavior changes when they exist.

8) Maintenance/rebuild utilities worth preserving conceptually
These are important because they reveal intended repair/reconciliation behavior:

INVCHK.ASC / LOGBSCAN.ASC: rebuild/check INVOICE.CHK from JOURNAL.CUR starting at a chosen invoice (INVCHK.ASC:1-21, LOGBSCAN.ASC:1-22).
LEDGSCAN.ASC: compare JOURNAL.CUR totals against INVOICE.CHK and log mismatches (LEDGSCAN.ASC:7-27).
LEDG-CHK.ASC: quick scan for malformed ledger amounts (LEDG-CHK.ASC:1-6).
JRNLSCAN.BAS: detect missing invoice numbers in JOURNAL.CUR (JRNLSCAN.BAS:1-17).
CHKCREAT.BAS / CHKCREA2.BAS: rebuild/verify BILLSCHK.DAT from BILLS.DAT (CHKCREA2.BAS:1-23, CHKCREAT.BAS:1-28).
SORTNAME.ASC / NAMEREDO.ASC: normalize/sort REALNAME.DAT and rename PRC files (SORTNAME.ASC:9-35, NAMEREDO.ASC:9-24).
BOOT.ASC: “print/update/void” admin menu that touches JOURNAL.CUR, LOGBOOK.yy, LEDGER, and price lists (BOOT.ASC:42-66, BOOT.ASC:101-205).
9) Practical guidance for WinForms continuation
If the goal is behavioral fidelity, I’d preserve these concepts exactly:

8-char customer code as the primary key
PRC price-list records as customer-specific procedure catalog
shopcard → invoice → journal/logbook/invoice-status pipeline
invoice status flags J/P/C/V/E
check posting as a separate flow that flips invoice flags and writes CHECK.INV
current-year LOGBOOK.yy rollover
explicit printer/workstation/environment flags
operator-facing uppercase workflow and low-trust validation prompts
Biggest migration risk: there is no single clean authoritative source tree. The repo contains live data plus overlapping BASIC generations, and some readable sources are older than the data/schema now present.

## Updated unified understanding

### 1. DOS app architecture is now much clearer
The AMi DOS system is a **DOS batch + GW-BASIC hub-and-spoke application**, not a single cohesive executable.

Top-level behavior:
- `AUTOEXEC.BAT` / `LOGIN.BAT` establish environment and mapped-drive assumptions
- the readable main router is effectively in `START.ASC`
- that menu branches into separate modules for:
  - shop cards
  - invoice generation
  - customer receipts / ledger
  - sales journal
  - logbook
  - pricing / PRC management
  - A/R inquiry (`ENTIRE`)
  - purchasing
  - vendor checks / cash disbursements (`BILL`)
  - maintenance / update / void flows (`BOOT`)

### 2. The real DOS “system of record” is a coordinated flat-file set
This scan reinforces that the DOS app depends on **multiple synchronized legacy files**, especially:

- `INVOICE.CHK`
- `LEDGER.CUR`
- `CHECK.INV`
- `JOURNAL.CUR`
- `LOGBOOK.yy`
- `OTHER.CHK`
- `PRC\*.PRC`
- `REALNAME.DAT`
- `PROCDURE.DAT`
- `COD.DAT`
- `COD-NO.DAT`
- `INVOICE.NUM`
- `LASTINVO.ICE`
- `MONTH.INV`

And it confirms a critical point:

### 3. `INVOICE.CHK` is central
It is the master invoice-status/index file with one-letter flags:
- `J` unpaid/open
- `P` paid
- `C` corrected cert
- `V` void
- `E` erased

That means any VB write-side parity work has to treat `INVOICE.CHK` as extremely high-risk and authoritative.

### 4. Customer payment / Add Check DOS behavior is now clearer
The DOS receipt-posting flow in `LEDGER.ASC`:
- validates invoice numbers against `INVOICE.CHK`
- rejects already-paid / corrected / void invoices
- flips invoice flags to `P`
- appends summary receipt data to `LEDGER.CUR`
- appends header + invoice-number list to `CHECK.INV`

That is hugely important, because it confirms that **Add Check is not just a form** — it is a coordinated multi-file transaction.

### 5. Delete Check parity is also clearly multi-file
DOS delete/void flow:
- removes or rebuilds matching receipt/linkage
- resets invoice flags back to unpaid
- keeps `LEDGER.CUR`, `CHECK.INV`, and `INVOICE.CHK` in sync

So if the VB port lacks a write pipeline, then both Add Check and Delete Check are still major parity gaps.

### 6. PRC/company semantics are confirmed as core behavior
This scan reinforces:
- customer IDs are 1–8 uppercase chars
- PRC filename stem is a key business identifier
- `REALNAME.DAT` maps abbreviation to long customer name
- `.PRC` files are a real operational dependency, not just archival data

That means `CompanyLookupService` in VB is useful groundwork, but **not full parity yet**.

### 7. Hidden DOS assumptions are now well established
This scan strongly confirms the behaviors that must be preserved or deliberately addressed:

- uppercase operator input
- 8-character customer codes
- mapped drive / DOS path assumptions
- printer/device assumptions (`LPT1`, `LPRINT`)
- GW/QB packed numeric semantics
- file locking / “someone is using your file” retry behavior

### 8. Source drift / duplicate-generation risk is real
This scan explicitly confirms:
- multiple overlapping invoice/source variants
- ledger format drift
- `MONTH.INV` schema mismatch
- shopcard writer/reader mismatch
- stale or partially superseded branches

So the DOS repo is **not a single clean canonical source tree**. That means:
- file data often matters as much as source code
- the VB continuation should be guided by **observed behavior + live file contracts**, not just one BASIC file in isolation

### What the VB port already does well

  - `FormAddChecks.vb`

### What is still the biggest missing milestone
A **true write-side accounting transaction engine** that preserves DOS semantics across:
- `INVOICE.CHK`

- `CHECK.INV`
- possibly `OTHER.CHK`

The latest state is probably:

1. **Read-side parity is strong**
2. **Sales Employee tooling exists but remains partial**

4. **True write-side accounting parity is still missing**

That is now the strongest continuity model I have.

## Best practical next-step conclusion
Given the DOS scan, my current best recommendation is:

### Treat `Add Check` as the primary real accounting path
Why:
- the DOS ledger/customer-receipt flow is a real coordinated transaction
- that is closer to the business core than the Sales Employee wizard
- Sales Employee flow may be better treated as specialized report/support workflow unless older notes prove otherwise

### So likely order of work should be
1. clarify whether Sales Employee wizard is report-only or intended to create checks
2. build the real Add Check writer-backed flow
3. then wire menu integration cleanly
4. then implement Delete Check / OTHER checks parity

# Updated version with split support
Here is a revised version of `Sync-ChatHistoryToRepo.ps1` that preserves existing behavior and adds markdown splitting.

```powershell
param(
    [switch]$Silent
)

$DailyBasePath = "H:\AM\DailyConversations"
$RepoPath = "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History"
$BranchName = "upload-chat-history"
$ChunkLineCount = 2000

function Split-TextFileIntoParts {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$SourceFile,

        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$OutputRoot,

        [int]$LinesPerPart = 2000
    )

    if (-not (Test-Path $SourceFile)) {
        return
    }

    $baseName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($SourceFile)
    $partsFolder = Join-Path $OutputRoot ($baseName + "_parts")

    if (-not (Test-Path $partsFolder)) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $partsFolder -Force | Out-Null
    }

    # Remove old generated parts so re-runs stay clean
    Get-ChildItem -Path $partsFolder -File -Filter "${baseName}_part_*.txt" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $partNumber = 1

    Get-Content -Path $SourceFile | ForEach-Object {
        $chunk.Add($_)

        if ($chunk.Count -ge $LinesPerPart) {
            $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
            $chunk | Set-Content -Path $partPath
            $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
            $partNumber++
        }
    }

    if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
        $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
        $chunk | Set-Content -Path $partPath
    }
}

$today = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
$monthFolder = (Get-Date).ToString("MMM-yyyy").ToLower()
$monthFolder = switch -Regex ($monthFolder) {
    '^jan-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jan', 'january' }
    '^feb-' { $monthFolder -replace '^feb', 'february' }
    '^mar-' { $monthFolder -replace '^mar', 'march' }
    '^apr-' { $monthFolder -replace '^apr', 'april' }
    '^may-' { $monthFolder -replace '^may', 'may' }
    '^jun-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jun', 'june' }
    '^jul-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jul', 'july' }
    '^aug-' { $monthFolder -replace '^aug', 'august' }
    '^sep-' { $monthFolder -replace '^sep', 'september' }
    '^oct-' { $monthFolder -replace '^oct', 'october' }
    '^nov-' { $monthFolder -replace '^nov', 'november' }
    '^dec-' { $monthFolder -replace '^dec', 'december' }
    default { $monthFolder }
}

$RepoSubfolder = "${monthFolder}-recovery\$today"
$TodayFolder = Join-Path $DailyBasePath $today
$RepoTargetFolder = Join-Path $RepoPath $RepoSubfolder

if (-not (Test-Path $TodayFolder)) {
    Write-Host "Today's source folder not found: $TodayFolder"
    exit 1
}

if (-not (Test-Path $RepoPath)) {
    Write-Host "Repo path not found: $RepoPath"
    exit 1
}

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $RepoTargetFolder -Force | Out-Null

# Copy today's master history file
$masterHistory = Join-Path $TodayFolder "${today}_master-history.md"
if (Test-Path $masterHistory) {
    Copy-Item -Path $masterHistory -Destination $RepoTargetFolder -Force
}

# Copy extracted files if they exist
$ExtractedRoot = Join-Path $TodayFolder "extracted"
if (Test-Path $ExtractedRoot) {
    $filesToCopy = Get-ChildItem -Path $ExtractedRoot -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object {
            $_.Extension.ToLower() -in ".md", ".json", ".txt"
        }

    foreach ($file in $filesToCopy) {
        Copy-Item -Path $file.FullName -Destination $RepoTargetFolder -Force
    }
}

# Split all markdown files in the repo target folder into companion text parts
$markdownFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoTargetFolder -File -Filter *.md -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($mdFile in $markdownFiles) {
    Split-TextFileIntoParts -SourceFile $mdFile.FullName -OutputRoot $RepoTargetFolder -LinesPerPart $ChunkLineCount
}

Push-Location $RepoPath

try {
    git checkout $BranchName
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Failed to checkout branch $BranchName"
    }

    git pull origin $BranchName
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Failed to pull branch $BranchName"
    }

    git add $RepoSubfolder

    $status = git status --porcelain
    if (-not $status) {
        Write-Host "No changes to commit."
        exit 0
    }

    $commitMessage = "Add chat history files for $today"
    git commit -m $commitMessage
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Git commit failed."
    }

    git push origin $BranchName
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Git push failed."
    }

    Write-Host "Synced chat history to repo: $RepoSubfolder"
}
finally {
    Pop-Location
}
```

# What this changes
This keeps your existing behavior and additionally:

- splits every `.md` copied into that day’s repo folder
- creates a sibling folder like:
  - `2026-05-20_master-history_parts`
- or:
  - `some_export_name_parts`
- places chunk files inside it

Example output:
```text
may-2026-recovery\2026-05-20\
  2026-05-20_master-history.md
  2026-05-20_master-history_parts\
    2026-05-20_master-history_part_001.txt
    2026-05-20_master-history_part_002.txt
```

---

# One thing to consider
Your current chunking by **line count** is simple and reliable, but it can still produce uneven file sizes if some lines are huge.

If you want, I can give you a **better version** that splits by approximate file size instead, which may be even better for repo readability.
