## @testsubject117

ok, since this is a new install of VB I need you to walk me through how to set this up correctly to publish how we were before. Right now I want to publish just a stand alone executable that can be copied to any workstation and run. I believe before we talked about it including .net 10, although I had to install .net 10 separately and manually on the virtual machine originally. if it's a huge hassle forget including .net.

## Copilot

Yes — for **“copy to any workstation and run”**, the simplest fit is a **self-contained Windows publish**. That bundles the .NET runtime with your app, so the target PC does **not** need .NET 10 installed separately. Single-file publishing is supported via `PublishSingleFile`; self-contained deployment bundles the runtime; and single-file apps are runtime/architecture-specific, e.g. `win-x64`. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

## My recommendation
Publish **self-contained + single-file + win-x64 + Release**.

That gives you:
- one `.exe` to copy,
- no separate .NET install on each workstation,
- easiest deployment for ad hoc workstation copies. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

If you decide you **don’t** want to include .NET, then publish **framework-dependent** instead. That makes a smaller output, but every workstation must already have the matching .NET desktop runtime installed. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

---

## Important expectation
Even with “single-file,” some apps may still emit extra files unless native libraries are set to self-extract/include appropriately. Microsoft documents `PublishSingleFile`, and Microsoft Q&A specifically calls out `IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true` when people expect one EXE but still see extra files. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

So the safest “old way” target is:

- `SelfContained = true`
- `PublishSingleFile = true`
- `RuntimeIdentifier = win-x64`
- `IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract = true`

---

# Easiest way: Visual Studio publish profile

## Option A: Use Visual Studio Publish UI
1. Open your project in Visual Studio.
2. In **Solution Explorer**, right-click the **startup WinForms project**.
3. Click **Publish**.
4. If prompted for a target, choose **Folder**.
5. Pick a folder like:
   `C:\Publish\AMiOffice`
6. Click **Finish**.

Then edit the publish settings:

7. In the Publish screen, click **Show all settings** or **Edit**.
8. Set:
   - **Configuration** = `Release`
   - **Target runtime** = `win-x64`
   - **Deployment mode** = `Self-contained`
   - **Produce single file** = `True`
9. If there is a checkbox for trimming, leave it **off** for a WinForms line-of-business app.
10. If there is a checkbox for ReadyToRun, you can leave it off unless you specifically want it.

Then click **Publish**. Visual Studio supports folder publishing for .NET desktop apps, including self-contained vs framework-dependent settings. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/deployment/quickstart-deploy-using-clickonce-folder?view=visualstudio&utm_source=openai))

---

# Best way if you want it predictable: edit the project file
If this is a new VB install and you want to stop guessing what Visual Studio remembered before, I recommend setting publish properties directly in the project file.

Open your `.vbproj` and add a property group like this:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <RuntimeIdentifier>win-x64</RuntimeIdentifier>
  <SelfContained>true</SelfContained>
  <PublishSingleFile>true</PublishSingleFile>
  <IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract>true</IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract>
</PropertyGroup>
```

These are the core properties Microsoft documents for single-file/self-contained publishing. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

## If your project already has publish settings
Merge carefully rather than duplicating conflicting properties.

---

# Command-line publish: most reliable
If you want the cleanest “do exactly this” publish, use Developer PowerShell or a terminal in the project folder:

```powershell
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true -o .\publish\win-x64
```

This uses the official `dotnet publish` flow with explicit self-contained and single-file settings. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

## What you should get
Look in:

```text
.\publish\win-x64
```

You should see your app EXE there.  
If everything cooperates, you may get just the EXE; if not, there may be a tiny number of companion files depending on app/native dependency behavior. Microsoft’s own docs and Q&A explain that nuance. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

---

# What I would do in your shoes
For **today’s release**, I would:

## Choice 1 — safest for users
Publish **self-contained**.

Use this command:

```powershell
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true -o .\publish\win-x64
```

Then test the EXE on:
- your dev machine,
- one workstation or VM that does **not** have your dev environment.

If it launches, you’re done. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

## Choice 2 — smallest package, but riskier
If bundling .NET turns into a hassle, use framework-dependent:

```powershell
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained false -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o .\publish\win-x64-fdd
```

But then each workstation must have the correct .NET desktop runtime already installed. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

---

# My advice on .NET 10
Since you said you previously had to manually install .NET 10 on the VM, I would **not rely on that** for random workstations. For a copy-and-run deployment, self-contained is the better fit because it includes the runtime with the app. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/project-sdk/msbuild-props?utm_source=openai))

So:
- **If you want least user friction:** include .NET via self-contained.
- **If you want smallest output and your environment is managed:** framework-dependent is OK.

---

# Things not to enable right now
For a business WinForms app, I would avoid these for the publish you’re doing today unless you’ve already tested them:
- trimming,
- AOT-style experiments,
- anything aggressive for size reduction.

Single-file + self-contained is enough for now. Microsoft’s single-file docs emphasize the core publish properties; trimming is a separate concern and can break reflection-heavy apps. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/single-file/overview?utm_source=openai))

---

# Quick step-by-step summary
## If you want the simplest route
1. Open terminal in the project folder.
2. Run:

```powershell
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true -o .\publish\win-x64
```

3. Go to `publish\win-x64`
4. Copy the EXE to a test machine.
5. Run it.

## @testsubject117

do I want to publish with clickonce?

## Copilot

No — **not for what you described**.

You said you want:
- a **standalone executable**
- that can be **copied to any workstation and run**

That is **not really a ClickOnce scenario**. ClickOnce is meant for **installing/updating** an app from a publish location like a folder share or website, with deployment manifests and versioned installs. Microsoft’s ClickOnce docs describe it as a deployment/install/update mechanism for Windows desktop apps, not just “make me one EXE I can copy around.” ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/deployment/quickstart-deploy-using-clickonce-folder?view=visualstudio&utm_source=openai))

## What you want instead
Use a **Folder publish**, not ClickOnce:
- **Release**
- **win-x64**
- **Self-contained**
- **Single file**

That matches your “copy to any workstation and run” goal much better, and self-contained publishing includes the .NET runtime so you don’t have to preinstall it on every machine. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/deployment/quickstart-deploy-using-clickonce-folder?view=visualstudio&utm_source=openai))

## Short rule of thumb
- **ClickOnce** = install/update experience
- **Folder publish** = copy files / copy EXE and run

For your case, choose **Folder publish**. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/deployment/quickstart-deploy-using-clickonce-folder?view=visualstudio&utm_source=openai))

## My recommendation
When Visual Studio asks:
- choose **Publish**
- choose **Folder**
- **do not choose ClickOnce**

Then set it to:
- **Self-contained**
- **Target runtime: win-x64**
- **Single file: On**

That will get you closest to the old “portable executable” style deployment. Self-contained single-file publishing is the .NET-supported approach for bundling app + runtime together. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/deployment/quickstart-deploy-using-clickonce-folder?view=visualstudio&utm_source=openai))

If you want, next I can give you the **exact click-by-click Visual Studio settings** to use on the Publish screen.

# 1. Executive Summary
Today’s work focused on finishing the remaining Checks-menu modernization items in **AMiWinForms**, while preserving the core DOS workflow, look, and operator expectations as closely as practical. The session centered heavily on the final Checks menu item, **(A) Find checks that don’t balance**, which was already functionally useful in VB but did not visually match the DOS-inspired UI used elsewhere in the application. The decision for today was explicitly **not** to rework the functional flow of `(A)` to match DOS exactly, because the DOS VM appears to currently do nothing when that item is selected and user confirmation is still pending. Instead, the agreed plan was to keep the existing useful VB implementation and restyle it so it fits the rest of the app. This preserves operator value now while deferring parity decisions until users clarify intended legacy behavior.

The active code file provided and revised was **`FormLedgerDoesntBalance.vb`**. That form already contained the business logic to load `LEDGER.CUR`, use `CHECK.INV` mappings, optionally resolve invoice amounts via `INVOICE.CHK`, and produce a list of checks that either have no invoice mapping or whose invoice totals do not balance to the check amount. The core logic uses `Tolerance = 1D`, preserving the DOS rule that differences under one dollar are treated as acceptable. The logic also distinguishes between “No CHECK.INV mapping” rows and actual delta rows with invoice mappings but imbalanced totals. We kept that behavior intact.

A major part of the work was re-skinning `FormLedgerDoesntBalance` to visually align with the existing DOS-like menu screens. The form was changed from a default WinForms look toward the app’s established style: dark charcoal/black background, large upper-left yellow **CHECKS** header, upper-right yellow date/time display, silver command buttons, dark grid, and DOS-inspired contrast. The command bar now includes **Refresh**, **Cancel**, **Copy Row**, **Export CSV**, and **(ESC) Close**. Keyboard handling was added so **Esc closes the form**. A header timer was introduced to keep the date/time clock updated. The ambiguous `Timer` compiler error occurred because both `System.Windows.Forms` and `System.Threading` were imported; this was fixed by explicitly declaring the timer as `System.Windows.Forms.Timer`.

The status/progress area for report generation also evolved during the session. Initially, the message such as **“Computing rows...”** plus the rolling count was placed on one line, and that text was visibly truncated in the UI. This was improved by splitting the progress into a two-line status area using two labels: one for the status message (for example, `Computing rows...`) and one below it for rolling counts (for example, `28,500/51,350`). That solved the truncation problem during computation and looked better in practice. However, after the computation completes and rows are displayed, there is still a residual visual issue where part of the earlier computing text appears to persist in the status area. This is not blocking release, but it was explicitly noted for tomorrow: either change the post-compute message to something clean like **“Report complete”** or **“Computations complete”**, or clear the transient computing message entirely.

Another refinement involved the results grid typography. After the first styling pass, the row text appeared too bold, which made the grid look heavy and odd. The solution was to make the **grid body regular-weight** while leaving the **column headers bold**. The row-prepaint logic had also been forcing some highlighted rows into bold; that was removed so highlighted rows remain regular-weight like the rest of the grid. This significantly improved readability and visual balance.

Color tuning was also adjusted in stages. Initially, the no-invoice rows were too gold/yellow and the mismatch rows too saturated pink/red. After seeing real screenshots, those colors were progressively softened. The final accepted look uses a **lighter pale yellow** for rows with no invoice mapping and a **soft milky pink** for mismatch/delta rows. The user explicitly confirmed that the latest yellow and pink now look fine and are acceptable for release.

We also discussed DOS parity implications of `(A) Find checks that don’t balance`. The DOS VM appears to do nothing when `(A)` is selected, and it is currently unknown whether that menu item ever actually worked in the legacy environment or if it was effectively dead/incomplete. Because of that uncertainty, the deliberate decision was to keep the VB version’s useful current behavior rather than disabling it or trying to force a speculative DOS flow. This is one of the important explicit deviations from strict DOS parity for now, but only provisionally; it needs follow-up with users.

Outside the form-specific work, we also discussed publishing/deployment because this was a new VB/Visual Studio setup after a crash/rebuild. The deployment goal was clarified as **a standalone executable that can be copied to any workstation and run**, not a ClickOnce installation workflow. Based on that, the recommendation was to use **Folder publish**, not ClickOnce, and preferably **self-contained + single-file + win-x64 + Release** so that the target workstation does not need a separate .NET runtime installation. The operator tested the published build on the VM and reported that it is **looking really good**. One forgotten infrastructure item surfaced at the end: previously there had been a **build counter** that incremented the build count by reading/writing a text file, but that was not restored after the crash. That now needs to be put back in place and was explicitly added to tomorrow’s task list.

In summary, today was a highly productive polish-and-release day. The Checks workflow is now substantially more consistent, `(A)` is visually integrated into the app while preserving its useful modernized behavior, and a publishable build has already been tested successfully on the VM. Tomorrow should focus on a small number of targeted cleanup items: the persistent/truncated “Computing...” status text behavior after completion, restoring the build counter increment mechanism, standardizing the Castellar/Castella title font across upper-left headers, and validating with users whether DOS `(A)` behavior was ever real or should remain a VB enhancement.

# 4. AMiDataStore Work Summary
There was **no new direct AMiDataStore code modification** performed in this session, but the session still touched AMiDataStore-related understanding indirectly through the form’s data access behavior and through the larger project framing.

## Data access behavior reviewed
The current `FormLedgerDoesntBalance` logic depends on legacy-style file readers and data access patterns that are part of the broader AMi data layer ecosystem:
- `LedgerCurReader.ReadAll(ledgerPath)`
- `CheckInvReader.ReadAll(checkInvPath)`
- `InvoiceChkReader.ReadRecord(invoiceChkPath, invNo)`
- `LegacyDataPaths.LedgerCur`
- `LegacyDataPaths.CheckInv`
- `LegacyDataPaths.InvoiceChk`
- `UiFileErrors.ShowMissingRequiredFile(...)`

These dependencies matter because they represent the modern VB/WinForms application’s bridge back to legacy DOS-era file structures and business workflows.

## Dependencies identified
The form depends on:
- ledger records from **`LEDGER.CUR`**
- check-to-invoice relationship data from **`CHECK.INV`**
- invoice amount lookups from **`INVOICE.CHK`**

The logic builds a composite key with:
- `Customer`
- `CheckNumber`

using `BuildKey(code, checkNum)`.

It then:
1. loads all ledger entries,
2. builds an in-memory index of check-to-invoice mappings,
3. resolves invoice amounts, caching them in `amtCache`,
4. identifies unbalanced or unmapped checks,
5. presents those as result rows.

## Repository interactions / implications
Even though no AMiDataStore repo tools were used in this session, the analysis confirms that AMiWinForms is still tightly dependent on datastore-level correctness and legacy-file semantics. The form’s output quality depends on:
- correct `CHECK.INV` parsing,
- correct invoice record resolution,
- correct handling of missing `INVOICE.CHK` entries,
- stable path resolution.

## Why those findings matter
This matters because `(A)` is not just a UI concern; its usefulness depends entirely on the fidelity of the file readers and mapping semantics. If users later challenge the output of the screen, debugging may need to move into AMiDataStore/file-reader territory. For now, the business rule path appears coherent enough that the form is worth shipping as a useful operator tool.

# 7. Key Technical Findings
- `FormLedgerDoesntBalance` is already structurally robust and includes async loading, cancellation, progress updates, filtering, export, and row copy features.
- Business-rule tolerance is explicitly defined as `Tolerance = 1D`, preserving a DOS-era “less than $1 difference is okay” rule.
- “No mapping” rows are produced when no `CHECK.INV` mapping exists for the `(Customer, CheckNumber)` key.
- Delta rows are produced when invoice totals do not match the check amount or when referenced invoices cannot be found in `INVOICE.CHK`.
- `ComputeRows(...)` uses a cached `amtCache` dictionary to avoid repeated invoice lookups for duplicate invoice numbers.
- `BuildKey(code, checkNum)` trims and composes `Customer|CheckNumber`, which is the critical mapping assumption for relationship resolution.
- The ambiguous `Timer` compile error happened because both `System.Windows.Forms` and `System.Threading` define `Timer`; explicit use of `System.Windows.Forms.Timer` fixes it.
- The initial single-line progress display caused truncation; splitting status and counts into two stacked labels is a cleaner and more resilient layout.
- The first two-line progress version was visually preferred by the operator.
- Bold body text in the `DataGridView` made the result grid look too heavy; regular body font is preferable.
- Highlight colors needed multiple tuning passes once real screenshots were visible; saturated gold/pink did not look right against the dark DOS-inspired styling.
- Current accepted colors are softer and better aligned to the app aesthetic.
- DOS VM behavior for `(A)` is currently unreliable as a baseline because it appears to do nothing.
- Publishing goal is **standalone executable deployment**, so **Folder publish** is the right model, not ClickOnce.
- Previous text-file-driven build counter was lost after the crash/rebuild and needs to be restored manually.

## Copilot

# 1. Executive Summary
Today’s work focused on closing out the remaining active Checks-menu polish item in the AMi modernization effort: **`(A) Find checks that don't balance`**, implemented in **`FormLedgerDoesntBalance.vb`** in **AMiWinForms**. The central decision was to keep the current VB logic for this feature, because it is already useful and appears to perform meaningful validation against legacy data files, even though the DOS VM currently appears to do nothing when `(A)` is selected. That DOS uncertainty means strict parity for this one item is still unresolved, so today’s work prioritized visual consistency and operator usability over speculative flow rewrites.

The starting point was a fully functioning WinForms report screen that already loaded ledger/check/invoice data and identified imbalance cases. The file provided by the operator was **`FormLedgerDoesntBalance.vb`**, which contains the following major logic components:
- **`RunReportAsync()`** for asynchronous report generation
- **`ComputeRows(...)`** for building mismatch rows
- **`ApplyFilterAndBind()`** for filter application and sorting
- **`dgv_RowPrePaint`** for row highlighting
- **`BuildKey(...)`**, **`SafeTrim(...)`**, **`SafeTrimEnd(...)`**, and **`Csv(...)`**
- nested helper types:
  - **`FilterMode`**
  - **`ProgressInfo`**
  - **`BalanceRow`**

The business logic in that form was intentionally preserved. It reads:
- **`LEDGER.CUR`** via `LedgerCurReader.ReadAll(...)`
- **`CHECK.INV`** via `CheckInvReader.ReadAll(...)`
- **`INVOICE.CHK`** via `InvoiceChkReader.ReadRecord(...)`

using paths from:
- **`LegacyDataPaths.LedgerCur`**
- **`LegacyDataPaths.CheckInv`**
- **`LegacyDataPaths.InvoiceChk`**

It then builds a composite customer/check key using `BuildKey(code, checkNum)`, indexes invoice mappings, resolves invoice amounts, caches invoice amounts in `amtCache`, and identifies two major categories of exceptions:
1. **No CHECK.INV mapping**
2. **Mapped checks whose invoice totals do not balance to the check amount**, including cases where invoice references exist but invoice records cannot be found

The tolerance rule stayed intact:
- **`Tolerance = 1D`**
which preserves the known DOS-era behavior that differences under one dollar are treated as acceptable.

The primary implementation work today was a styling and usability pass on `FormLedgerDoesntBalance` so it would look more like the rest of the DOS-inspired application rather than like a generic Windows utility form. The screen was changed to include:
- dark charcoal/black background
- black top header area
- upper-left large yellow **CHECKS** title
- upper-right yellow date/time clock
- silver toolbar buttons
- darker `DataGridView`
- `(ESC) Close` button and keyboard support
- DOS-like visual treatment overall

An explicit compile/debug issue came up when adding the clock: **`Timer`** was ambiguous because both `System.Windows.Forms` and `System.Threading` were imported. That was resolved by explicitly using:
- **`System.Windows.Forms.Timer`**

Another UI issue involved the progress display during report generation. Initially, the status line showed something like **“Computing rows... (28,500/51,350)”** all on one line, which was visibly truncated. The fix was to split that into a **two-line status block**:
- top line = status message, e.g. `Computing rows...`
- bottom line = rolling numbers, e.g. `28,500/51,350`

This version was preferred by the operator and looked better in practice. However, after computation completed and the grid displayed results, part of the old **“Computing...”** message still appeared to remain in the status area. That is not blocking release, but it is explicitly on the list for tomorrow to either:
- change to **“Report complete”** / **“Computations complete”**, or
- clear the transient computation text entirely

A visual refinement was also needed for the grid body text. The initial styled version left all result rows looking bold, which made the list too heavy. The grid body was updated to use **regular-weight** text while keeping **column headers bold**. Forced bold formatting on highlighted rows was also removed.

Row highlight colors then went through several iterations based on actual screenshots. Originally:
- the no-invoice rows looked too gold/saturated yellow
- the mismatch rows looked too strong/pastel-pink-red

These were softened multiple times until the operator approved the final look:
- **lighter pale yellow** for rows with no invoice mapping
- **soft milky pink** for rows with invoice deltas

The operator ultimately confirmed that the latest yellow and pink look fine.

Another important near-future cleanup item was identified: the upper-left **CHECKS** title font in this form is still only an approximation and does **not** match the exact **Castellar/Castella-style font** used on the Main Menu and Checks Menu. This needs to be standardized so all upper-left header titles across DOS-styled forms use the same exact font definition and size.

Publishing and deployment were also discussed because this is a rebuilt Visual Studio/VB environment after a crash. The operator wanted to publish a build as a **standalone executable** that could be copied to workstations and run. We clarified that:
- **ClickOnce is not appropriate** for that goal
- **Folder publish** is the correct approach
- ideally use **self-contained + single-file + win-x64 + Release** if minimizing workstation runtime dependencies is important

The operator did publish a build and test it on the virtual machine, and reported that it is **looking really good**.

At the end of the session, one additional infrastructure item surfaced: there had previously been a **build counter** that incremented a build number by reading/updating a text file, but that mechanism was apparently not restored after the crash/rebuild. That now needs to be reinstated. This was explicitly added to tomorrow’s list, along with:
- the status cleanup after computation
- title font standardization
- validating with users whether DOS `(A)` ever actually did anything

Overall, today was a productive closeout/polish/release session. The current build is good enough to publish, the VM run looks good, and the remaining work is now a focused set of small cleanup items plus one open product question about DOS parity for `(A)`.

# 3. Key Technical Findings
- **`FormLedgerDoesntBalance.vb`** is already a substantial functional implementation, not just a UI shell.
- The core business logic is organized around:
  - `RunReportAsync()`
  - `ComputeRows(...)`
  - `ApplyFilterAndBind()`
  - `dgv_RowPrePaint`
- The form distinguishes between:
  - rows with **no CHECK.INV mapping**
  - rows with **invoice mappings whose totals do not match the check amount**
- `ComputeRows(...)` uses a cache:
  - `Dim amtCache As New Dictionary(Of Long, Decimal)()`
  to avoid repeatedly reading invoice records for duplicate invoice references.
- The composite relationship key is built using:
  - `BuildKey(code, checkNum) = trimmed customer code + "|" + trimmed check number`
- Missing `CHECK.INV` data causes rows to be flagged as:
  - `"No CHECK.INV mapping"`
- Missing invoice records in `INVOICE.CHK` cause rows to be flagged via note text:
  - `"Invoices not found in INVOICE.CHK"`
- The logic currently considers a row unbalanced when:
  - no mapped invoice amounts were found, or
  - `Math.Abs(delta) >= Tolerance`
- The DOS-era tolerance assumption remains baked into:
  - `Private Const Tolerance As Decimal = 1D`
- The initial one-line progress/status message was too wide for the command bar and got truncated.
- Splitting progress into two labels was a cleaner design:
  - status message on top
  - counts below
- The operator preferred the first split-label implementation visually.
- Ambiguous timer issue occurred because of:
  - `Imports System.Windows.Forms`
  - `Imports System.Threading`
  and both namespaces expose a `Timer`.
- Correct fix was to explicitly declare:
  - `Private ReadOnly tmrClock As System.Windows.Forms.Timer = New System.Windows.Forms.Timer()`
- `DataGridView` body text looked too heavy when styled bold; regular body font is visually preferable.
- Highlight colors had to be tuned in the context of the dark DOS-like theme; saturated gold/pink felt wrong.
- The final accepted visual treatment uses much lighter, softer pastel highlighting.
- Current title font in this form still uses an approximation and does not match the title font used on the Main Menu / Checks Menu.
- The app was successfully published and tested on the VM.
- The previous automated/incremental build-counter mechanism is missing after the crash/rebuild and needs restoration.

## @testsubject117

```
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [string]$SourceFile,

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [string]$RepoPath,

    [int]$ChunkSize = 2000
)

$baseName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($SourceFile)
$outDir = Join-Path $RepoPath ($baseName + "_parts")

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outDir | Out-Null

$i = 1
$chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]

Get-Content $SourceFile | ForEach-Object {
    $chunk.Add($_)
    if ($chunk.Count -ge $ChunkSize) {
        $file = Join-Path $outDir ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $i)
        $chunk | Set-Content $file
        $i++
        $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    }
}

if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
    $file = Join-Path $outDir ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $i)
    $chunk | Set-Content $file
}

Write-Host "Created split files in: $outDir"
Get-ChildItem $outDir | Select-Object Name, Length
```
ok, lets have you review the script and tell me what it does and where the files are that need to be split, or where they are if they are already split: 

## Copilot

This script **only splits one file you explicitly point it at**. It does **not** scan Downloads, does **not** auto-find `.md`/`.json` files, and does **not** push anything to GitHub.

## What it does
It takes:

- `-SourceFile`
- `-RepoPath`
- optional `-ChunkSize` defaulting to `2000`

Then it:

1. gets the source filename without extension
2. creates an output folder inside the repo path named:

```text
<baseName>_parts
```

3. reads the source file line-by-line
4. groups lines into chunks of 2000
5. writes each chunk as:

```text
<baseName>_part_001.txt
<baseName>_part_002.txt
...
```

6. prints the output folder and the files created

---

# Example
If you ran:

```powershell
.\Split-ChatFile.ps1 `
  -SourceFile "C:\Users\You\Downloads\wed_may_20_2026_some_chat.md" `
  -RepoPath "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History"
```

it would create:

```text
E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History\wed_may_20_2026_some_chat_parts\
```

with files like:

```text
wed_may_20_2026_some_chat_part_001.txt
wed_may_20_2026_some_chat_part_002.txt
```

---

# Important conclusion
So if you expected this script to:
- scan Downloads,
- find new `.md` or `.json`,
- save them into the repo,
- split them,
- commit and push them,

then this is **not that script**.

This script is only the **splitter** step.

```
param(
    [switch]$Silent
)

$BasePath = "H:\AM\DailyConversations"
$ScanPaths = @(
    "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads",
    "H:\AM\Backed up CoPilot Sessions"
)

function Get-VersionNumber {
    param([string]$FileName)

    if ($FileName -match '\((\d+)\)(?=\.[^.]+$)') {
        return [int]$matches[1]
    }

    return 0
}

function Get-NormalizedBaseName {
    param([string]$FileName)

    $nameWithoutExtension = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($FileName)
    $normalized = $nameWithoutExtension -replace '\s*\(\d+\)$', ''
    return $normalized.ToLower()
}

function Get-TodayExportFiles {
    param([string[]]$Paths)

    $now = Get-Date

    $datePatterns = @(
        $now.ToString("ddd_MMM_d_yyyy"),
        $now.ToString("ddd_MMMM_d_yyyy"),
        $now.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd"),
        $now.ToString("MM-dd-yyyy"),
        $now.ToString("M-d-yyyy")
    ) | ForEach-Object {
        $_.ToLower().Replace("-", "_").Replace(" ", "_")
    }

    $results = @()

    foreach ($path in $Paths) {
        if (-not (Test-Path $path)) {
            continue
        }

        $files = Get-ChildItem -Path $path -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object {
                $_.Extension.ToLower() -in ".md", ".json", ".zip"
            } |
            Where-Object {
                $baseName = $_.BaseName.ToLower().Replace("-", "_").Replace(" ", "_")
                ($datePatterns | Where-Object { $baseName -like "*$_*" }).Count -gt 0
            }

        $results += $files
    }

    return $results
}

function Get-LatestExportGroup {
    param([System.IO.FileInfo[]]$Files)

    if (-not $Files -or $Files.Count -eq 0) {
        return $null
    }

    $ranked = $Files |
        Sort-Object `
            @{ Expression = { Get-VersionNumber $_.Name }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true }

    $best = $ranked | Select-Object -First 1
    $bestNormalized = Get-NormalizedBaseName $best.Name
    $bestVersion = Get-VersionNumber $best.Name

    $group = $Files | Where-Object {
        (Get-NormalizedBaseName $_.Name) -eq $bestNormalized -and
        (Get-VersionNumber $_.Name) -eq $bestVersion
    }

    return $group
}

function Expand-ZipFile {
    param(
        [System.IO.FileInfo]$ZipFile,
        [string]$DestinationRoot
    )

    $extractFolderName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($ZipFile.Name)
    $extractPath = Join-Path $DestinationRoot $extractFolderName

    if (Test-Path $extractPath) {
        Remove-Item -Path $extractPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $extractPath -Force | Out-Null
    Expand-Archive -Path $ZipFile.FullName -DestinationPath $extractPath -Force

    return $extractPath
}

function Get-MainMarkdownCandidate {
    param(
        [System.IO.FileInfo[]]$MarkdownFiles,
        [string]$ExpectedBaseName
    )

    if (-not $MarkdownFiles -or $MarkdownFiles.Count -eq 0) {
        return $null
    }

    $expected = $ExpectedBaseName.ToLower()

    $ranked = $MarkdownFiles |
        Sort-Object `
            @{ Expression = {
                $name = $_.BaseName.ToLower()
                if ($name -eq $expected) { 100 }
                elseif ($name -like "$expected*") { 90 }
                elseif ($name -match 'checklist|readme|guide|instruction|instructions') { 10 }
                else { 50 }
            }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.Length }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true }

    return $ranked | Select-Object -First 1
}

function Get-BestImportSourceFromGroup {
    param(
        [System.IO.FileInfo[]]$GroupFiles,
        [string]$TodayFolder
    )

    if (-not $GroupFiles -or $GroupFiles.Count -eq 0) {
        return $null
    }

    $zipFile = $GroupFiles |
        Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".zip" } |
        Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1

    if ($zipFile) {
        $extractRoot = Join-Path $TodayFolder "extracted"
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $extractRoot -Force | Out-Null

        $extractPath = Expand-ZipFile -ZipFile $zipFile -DestinationRoot $extractRoot
        $expectedBaseName = Get-NormalizedBaseName $zipFile.Name

        $mdFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $extractPath -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".md" }

        $mdInside = Get-MainMarkdownCandidate -MarkdownFiles $mdFiles -ExpectedBaseName $expectedBaseName

        if ($mdInside) {
            return [PSCustomObject]@{
                SourceType    = "ExtractedMarkdown"
                ImportFile    = $mdInside
                ContainerFile = $zipFile
                ExtractPath   = $extractPath
            }
        }

        $jsonInside = Get-ChildItem -Path $extractPath -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".json" } |
            Sort-Object `
                @{ Expression = { $_.Length }; Descending = $true },
                @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true } |
            Select-Object -First 1

        if ($jsonInside) {
            return [PSCustomObject]@{
                SourceType    = "ExtractedJson"
                ImportFile    = $jsonInside
                ContainerFile = $zipFile
                ExtractPath   = $extractPath
            }
        }
    }

    $standaloneMdFiles = $GroupFiles |
        Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".md" }

    $expectedStandaloneBase = if ($GroupFiles.Count -gt 0) {
        Get-NormalizedBaseName $GroupFiles[0].Name
    } else {
        ""
    }

    $standaloneMd = Get-MainMarkdownCandidate -MarkdownFiles $standaloneMdFiles -ExpectedBaseName $expectedStandaloneBase

    if ($standaloneMd) {
        return [PSCustomObject]@{
            SourceType    = "StandaloneMarkdown"
            ImportFile    = $standaloneMd
            ContainerFile = $null
            ExtractPath   = $null
        }
    }

    $standaloneJson = $GroupFiles |
        Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".json" } |
        Sort-Object `
            @{ Expression = { $_.Length }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true } |
        Select-Object -First 1

    if ($standaloneJson) {
        return [PSCustomObject]@{
            SourceType    = "StandaloneJson"
            ImportFile    = $standaloneJson
            ContainerFile = $null
            ExtractPath   = $null
        }
    }

    return $null
}

function Get-LatestPreviousHistoryFile {
    param([string]$BasePath, [string]$Today)

    $previousFolder = Get-ChildItem -Path $BasePath -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $_.Name -lt $Today } |
        Sort-Object Name -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1

    if (-not $previousFolder) {
        return $null
    }

    $previousFile = Get-ChildItem -Path $previousFolder.FullName -File -Filter "*_master-history.md" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1

    return $previousFile
}

$now = Get-Date
$today = $now.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
$todayFolder = Join-Path $BasePath $today
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $todayFolder -Force | Out-Null

$historyFile = Join-Path $todayFolder "${today}_master-history.md"
$previousHistory = Get-LatestPreviousHistoryFile -BasePath $BasePath -Today $today

$todayExports = Get-TodayExportFiles -Paths $ScanPaths
$latestGroup = Get-LatestExportGroup -Files $todayExports
$importSource = Get-BestImportSourceFromGroup -GroupFiles $latestGroup -TodayFolder $todayFolder

$latestImportSource = if ($importSource) { $importSource.ImportFile.FullName } else { "None" }

$content = @()
$content += "# Daily Copilot Running History"
$content += ""
$content += "- Date: $($now.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))"
$content += "- Last Updated: $($now.ToString('HH:mm:ss'))"
$content += "- Latest Import Source: $latestImportSource"
$content += ""

if ($importSource) {
    $content += "- Import Source Type: $($importSource.SourceType)"
    if ($importSource.ContainerFile) {
        $content += "- Source Archive: $($importSource.ContainerFile.FullName)"
    }
    if ($importSource.ExtractPath) {
        $content += "- Extracted To: $($importSource.ExtractPath)"
    }
    $content += ""
}

$content += "---"
$content += ""

$content += "## Previous Running History"
$content += ""

if ($previousHistory) {
    $content += Get-Content -Path $previousHistory.FullName
}
else {
    $content += "_No previous running history file was found._"
}

$content += ""
$content += "---"
$content += ""

$content += "## Today's Latest Export"
$content += ""

if ($importSource) {
    $detectedVersionSource = if ($importSource.ContainerFile) { $importSource.ContainerFile.Name } else { $importSource.ImportFile.Name }

    $content += "- Source File: $($importSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
    $content += "- Last Write Time: $($importSource.ImportFile.LastWriteTime)"
    $content += "- File Type: $($importSource.ImportFile.Extension)"
    $content += "- Detected Version: $(Get-VersionNumber $detectedVersionSource)"
    $content += ""
    $content += "===== BEGIN IMPORTED EXPORT ====="
    $content += ""

    try {
        $raw = Get-Content -Path $importSource.ImportFile.FullName -Raw -ErrorAction Stop
        $content += $raw
    }
    catch {
        $content += "[ERROR] Failed to read import file: $($importSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
        $content += $_.Exception.Message
    }

    $content += ""
    $content += "===== END IMPORTED EXPORT ====="
}
else {
    $content += "_No export file for today was found in the scan paths._"
}

$content += ""
$content += "---"
$content += ""
$content += "## New Notes"
$content += ""
$content += "_Add today's notes below._"
$content += ""

Set-Content -Path $historyFile -Value $content -Encoding UTF8

if (-not $Silent) {
    Start-Process notepad.exe $historyFile
}

Write-Host "Updated: $historyFile"
if ($importSource) {
    Write-Host "Imported from: $($importSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
    Write-Host "Import type: $($importSource.SourceType)"
    if ($importSource.ContainerFile) {
        Write-Host "Archive source: $($importSource.ContainerFile.FullName)"
    }
}
else {
    Write-Host "No export found for today."
}
```

So this script is a **history-builder/importer**, not the uploader/splitter/pusher.

# What this script does

## Inputs
Only one optional parameter:

```powershell
[switch]$Silent
```

If `-Silent` is not used, it opens the generated file in Notepad.

and inside that it writes:

# How it finds “today’s” files
Function:
```powershell
Get-TodayExportFiles
```

It only looks for files with these extensions:

```powershell
.md
.json
.zip
```

And it only keeps files whose names appear to include **today’s date** in one of these formats:

- `ddd_MMM_d_yyyy`
- `ddd_MMMM_d_yyyy`
- `yyyy-MM-dd`
- `MM-dd-yyyy`
- `M-d-yyyy`

Then it normalizes them by lowercasing and replacing spaces/hyphens with underscores.

## Important implication
If your file is named something like:

```text

```

this script would only find it if the script was run on **May 20, 2026**, because it uses:


and searches only for **today’s** date.

# How it picks the “best” file group
It groups versions like:
- `file.md`
- `file (1).md`
- `file (2).md`

and prefers the highest `(n)` version.

Functions involved:
- `Get-VersionNumber`
- `Get-NormalizedBaseName`
- `Get-LatestExportGroup`

So if both existed:
- `wed_may_20_2026_chat.md`
- `wed_may_20_2026_chat (2).md`

it would prefer version `(2)`.

# How it chooses what to import
Function:
```powershell
Get-BestImportSourceFromGroup
```

Priority is roughly:

## if there is a zip
- extract the zip into:

```text
H:\AM\DailyConversations\<today>\extracted\<zip-name>\
```

- prefer a good markdown candidate inside
- otherwise prefer a large json inside

## if no zip
- prefer a standalone markdown file
- otherwise prefer a standalone json file

It builds:

```text
H:\AM\DailyConversations\<today>\<today>_master-history.md
```

For example, on May 21:

That file contains:

```
param(
    [switch]$Silent
)

$DailyBasePath = "H:\AM\DailyConversations"
$RepoPath = "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History"
$BranchName = "upload-chat-history"
$ChunkLineCount = 2000

function Split-TextFileIntoParts {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$SourceFile,

        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$OutputRoot,

        [int]$LinesPerPart = 2000
    )

    if (-not (Test-Path $SourceFile)) {
        return
    }

    $baseName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($SourceFile)
    $partsFolder = Join-Path $OutputRoot ($baseName + "_parts")

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $partsFolder -Force | Out-Null

    Get-ChildItem -Path $partsFolder -File -Filter "${baseName}_part_*.txt" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $partNumber = 1

    Get-Content -Path $SourceFile | ForEach-Object {
        $chunk.Add($_)

        if ($chunk.Count -ge $LinesPerPart) {
            $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
            $chunk | Set-Content -Path $partPath -Encoding UTF8
            $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
            $partNumber++
        }
    }

    if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
        $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
        $chunk | Set-Content -Path $partPath -Encoding UTF8
    }
}

$today = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
$monthFolder = (Get-Date).ToString("MMM-yyyy").ToLower()
$monthFolder = switch -Regex ($monthFolder) {
    '^jan-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jan', 'january' }
    '^feb-' { $monthFolder -replace '^feb', 'february' }
    '^mar-' { $monthFolder -replace '^mar', 'march' }
    '^apr-' { $monthFolder -replace '^apr', 'april' }
    '^may-' { $monthFolder -replace '^may', 'may' }
    '^jun-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jun', 'june' }
    '^jul-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jul', 'july' }
    '^aug-' { $monthFolder -replace '^aug', 'august' }
    '^sep-' { $monthFolder -replace '^sep', 'september' }
    '^oct-' { $monthFolder -replace '^oct', 'october' }
    '^nov-' { $monthFolder -replace '^nov', 'november' }
    '^dec-' { $monthFolder -replace '^dec', 'december' }
    default { $monthFolder }
}

$RepoSubfolder = "${monthFolder}-recovery\$today"
$TodayFolder = Join-Path $DailyBasePath $today
$RepoTargetFolder = Join-Path $RepoPath $RepoSubfolder

if (-not (Test-Path $TodayFolder)) {
    Write-Host "Today's source folder not found: $TodayFolder"
    exit 1
}

if (-not (Test-Path $RepoPath)) {
    Write-Host "Repo path not found: $RepoPath"
    exit 1
}

Push-Location $RepoPath

try {
    git checkout $BranchName
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Failed to checkout branch $BranchName"
    }

    git pull origin $BranchName
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Failed to pull branch $BranchName"
    }

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $RepoTargetFolder -Force | Out-Null

    $masterHistory = Join-Path $TodayFolder "${today}_master-history.md"
    if (Test-Path $masterHistory) {
        Copy-Item -Path $masterHistory -Destination $RepoTargetFolder -Force
    }

    $ExtractedRoot = Join-Path $TodayFolder "extracted"
    if (Test-Path $ExtractedRoot) {
        $filesToCopy = Get-ChildItem -Path $ExtractedRoot -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object {
                $_.Extension.ToLower() -in ".md", ".json", ".txt"
            }

        foreach ($file in $filesToCopy) {
            Copy-Item -Path $file.FullName -Destination $RepoTargetFolder -Force
        }
    }

    $markdownFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoTargetFolder -File -Filter *.md -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    foreach ($mdFile in $markdownFiles) {
        Split-TextFileIntoParts -SourceFile $mdFile.FullName -OutputRoot $RepoTargetFolder -LinesPerPart $ChunkLineCount
    }

    git add $RepoSubfolder

    $status = git status --porcelain
    if (-not $status) {
        Write-Host "No changes to commit."
        exit 0
    }

    $commitMessage = "Add chat history files for $today"
    git commit -m $commitMessage
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Git commit failed."
    }

    git push origin $BranchName
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Git push failed."
    }

    Write-Host "Synced chat history to repo: $RepoSubfolder"
}
finally {
    Pop-Location
}
```

# Why the May 20 file is probably missing
Now that we can see the full pipeline, the likely failure point is much clearer.

## Most likely cause
These scripts are **date-driven using `Get-Date`**.

That means:
- script 1 only looks for **today’s** exports
- script 3 only syncs **today’s** folder

So if the May 20 chat export existed, but:
- script 1 was run on May 21,
- or script 3 was run on May 21,

then the system would operate on:

```text
2026-05-21
```

not:

```text
2026-05-20
```

That would absolutely explain why you expected a `wed_may_20_2026...` result but do not see it in the repo.

---

# Critical design limitation
The automation is built around:

```powershell
$today = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd"
```

in the repo sync script and similar “today-only” logic in the importer script.

That means it is **not robust for late processing**.

If the export file is from yesterday, this chain can miss it entirely or write it into the wrong day’s folder.

---

# What this 3rd script writes to the repo
For today, it would write into:

```text
E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History\may-2026-recovery\2026-05-21\
```

not a root-level file like:

```text
wed_may_20_2026_...
```

So another reason you may not have seen it is that the newer automation stores files in **dated subfolders**, not necessarily with the old naming pattern at the repo root.

## Direct answer
The next step is to split that large markdown file into parts, because at ~31.7 MB it’s too large/unwieldy to rely on as a single file for review.

## Do this now: split the master history into parts
Use this PowerShell block directly:

```powershell
$SourceFile = "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History\may-2026-recovery\2026-05-20\2026-05-20_master-history.md"
$OutputRoot = "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History\may-2026-recovery\2026-05-20"
$LinesPerPart = 2000

$baseName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($SourceFile)
$partsFolder = Join-Path $OutputRoot ($baseName + "_parts")

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $partsFolder -Force | Out-Null

Get-ChildItem $partsFolder -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Name -like "${baseName}_part_*.txt" } |
  Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

$chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$partNumber = 1

Get-Content $SourceFile | ForEach-Object {
    $chunk.Add($_)

    if ($chunk.Count -ge $LinesPerPart) {
        $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
        $chunk | Set-Content $partPath -Encoding UTF8
        $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
        $partNumber++
    }
}

if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
    $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
    $chunk | Set-Content $partPath -Encoding UTF8
}

Get-ChildItem $partsFolder |
  Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime
```

Yes — here’s a single robust script that merges the 3 flows into one and fixes the main issues we found: hardcoded repo path, “today only” brittleness, and fragmented steps. It uses PowerShell parameter validation patterns supported by PowerShell advanced functions and validation attributes. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/developer/cmdlet/validating-parameter-input?view=powershell-7.5&utm_source=openai))

````powershell name=Sync-CopilotChatHistory.ps1
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [ValidateScript({ Test-Path $_ })]
    [string]$RepoPath,

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [datetime]$TargetDate = (Get-Date),

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [string]$DailyBasePath = "H:\AM\DailyConversations",

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [string[]]$ScanPaths = @(
        "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads",
        "H:\AM\Backed up CoPilot Sessions"
    ),

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [string]$BranchName = "upload-chat-history",

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [ValidateRange(100, 10000)]
    [int]$ChunkLineCount = 2000,

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [switch]$SkipGit,

    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
    [switch]$Silent
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Write-Info {
    param([string]$Message)
    Write-Host "[INFO] $Message"
}

function Get-VersionNumber {
    param([string]$FileName)

    if ($FileName -match '\((\d+)\)(?=\.[^.]+$)') {
        return [int]$matches[1]
    }

    return 0
}

function Get-NormalizedBaseName {
    param([string]$FileName)

    $nameWithoutExtension = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($FileName)
    $normalized = $nameWithoutExtension -replace '\s*\(\d+\)$', ''
    return $normalized.ToLower().Replace("-", "_").Replace(" ", "_")
}

function Get-DatePatterns {
    param([datetime]$Date)

    return @(
        $Date.ToString("ddd_MMM_d_yyyy"),
        $Date.ToString("ddd_MMMM_d_yyyy"),
        $Date.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd"),
        $Date.ToString("MM-dd-yyyy"),
        $Date.ToString("M-d-yyyy")
    ) | ForEach-Object {
        $_.ToLower().Replace("-", "_").Replace(" ", "_")
    }
}

function Get-ExportFilesForDate {
    param(
        [string[]]$Paths,
        [datetime]$Date
    )

    $datePatterns = Get-DatePatterns -Date $Date
    $results = @()

    foreach ($path in $Paths) {
        if (-not (Test-Path $path)) {
            continue
        }

        $files = Get-ChildItem -Path $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer } |
            Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -in ".md", ".json", ".zip" } |
            Where-Object {
                $baseName = $_.BaseName.ToLower().Replace("-", "_").Replace(" ", "_")
                ($datePatterns | Where-Object { $baseName -like "*$_*" }).Count -gt 0
            }

        $results += $files
    }

    return $results
}

function Get-LatestExportGroup {
    param([object[]]$Files)

    if (-not $Files -or $Files.Count -eq 0) {
        return $null
    }

    $ranked = $Files |
        Sort-Object `
            @{ Expression = { Get-VersionNumber $_.Name }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true }

    $best = $ranked | Select-Object -First 1
    $bestNormalized = Get-NormalizedBaseName $best.Name
    $bestVersion = Get-VersionNumber $best.Name

    return $Files | Where-Object {
        (Get-NormalizedBaseName $_.Name) -eq $bestNormalized -and
        (Get-VersionNumber $_.Name) -eq $bestVersion
    }
}

function Expand-ZipFile {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [object]$ZipFile,

        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$DestinationRoot
    )

    $extractFolderName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($ZipFile.Name)
    $extractPath = Join-Path $DestinationRoot $extractFolderName

    if (Test-Path $extractPath) {
        Remove-Item -Path $extractPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $extractPath -Force | Out-Null
    Expand-Archive -Path $ZipFile.FullName -DestinationPath $extractPath -Force

    return $extractPath
}

function Get-MainMarkdownCandidate {
    param(
        [object[]]$MarkdownFiles,
        [string]$ExpectedBaseName
    )

    if (-not $MarkdownFiles -or $MarkdownFiles.Count -eq 0) {
        return $null
    }

    $expected = $ExpectedBaseName.ToLower()

    $ranked = $MarkdownFiles |
        Sort-Object `
            @{ Expression = {
                $name = $_.BaseName.ToLower()
                if ($name -eq $expected) { 100 }
                elseif ($name -like "$expected*") { 90 }
                elseif ($name -match 'checklist|readme|guide|instruction|instructions') { 10 }
                else { 50 }
            }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.Length }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true }

    return $ranked | Select-Object -First 1
}

function Get-BestImportSourceFromGroup {
    param(
        [object[]]$GroupFiles,
        [string]$TodayFolder
    )

    if (-not $GroupFiles -or $GroupFiles.Count -eq 0) {
        return $null
    }

    $zipFile = $GroupFiles |
        Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".zip" } |
        Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1

    if ($zipFile) {
        $extractRoot = Join-Path $TodayFolder "extracted"
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $extractRoot -Force | Out-Null

        $extractPath = Expand-ZipFile -ZipFile $zipFile -DestinationRoot $extractRoot
        $expectedBaseName = Get-NormalizedBaseName $zipFile.Name

        $mdFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $extractPath -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".md" }

        $mdInside = Get-MainMarkdownCandidate -MarkdownFiles $mdFiles -ExpectedBaseName $expectedBaseName
        if ($mdInside) {
            return [PSCustomObject]@{
                SourceType    = "ExtractedMarkdown"
                ImportFile    = $mdInside
                ContainerFile = $zipFile
                ExtractPath   = $extractPath
            }
        }

        $jsonInside = Get-ChildItem -Path $extractPath -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".json" } |
            Sort-Object `
                @{ Expression = { $_.Length }; Descending = $true },
                @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true } |
            Select-Object -First 1

        if ($jsonInside) {
            return [PSCustomObject]@{
                SourceType    = "ExtractedJson"
                ImportFile    = $jsonInside
                ContainerFile = $zipFile
                ExtractPath   = $extractPath
            }
        }
    }

    $standaloneMdFiles = $GroupFiles |
        Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".md" }

    $expectedStandaloneBase = Get-NormalizedBaseName (($GroupFiles | Select-Object -First 1).Name)
    $standaloneMd = Get-MainMarkdownCandidate -MarkdownFiles $standaloneMdFiles -ExpectedBaseName $expectedStandaloneBase

    if ($standaloneMd) {
        return [PSCustomObject]@{
            SourceType    = "StandaloneMarkdown"
            ImportFile    = $standaloneMd
            ContainerFile = $null
            ExtractPath   = $null
        }
    }

    $standaloneJson = $GroupFiles |
        Where-Object { $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".json" } |
        Sort-Object `
            @{ Expression = { $_.Length }; Descending = $true },
            @{ Expression = { $_.LastWriteTime }; Descending = $true } |
        Select-Object -First 1

    if ($standaloneJson) {
        return [PSCustomObject]@{
            SourceType    = "StandaloneJson"
            ImportFile    = $standaloneJson
            ContainerFile = $null
            ExtractPath   = $null
        }
    }

    return $null
}

function Get-LatestPreviousHistoryFile {
    param(
        [string]$BasePath,
        [string]$Today
    )

    $previousFolder = Get-ChildItem -Path $BasePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Name -lt $Today } |
        Sort-Object Name -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1

    if (-not $previousFolder) {
        return $null
    }

    return Get-ChildItem -Path $previousFolder.FullName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Name -like "*_master-history.md" } |
        Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
        Select-Object -First 1
}

function Build-MasterHistoryFile {
    param(
        [datetime]$Date,
        [string]$DailyBasePath,
        [object]$ImportSource
    )

    $today = $Date.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
    $todayFolder = Join-Path $DailyBasePath $today
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $todayFolder -Force | Out-Null

    $historyFile = Join-Path $todayFolder "${today}_master-history.md"
    $previousHistory = Get-LatestPreviousHistoryFile -BasePath $DailyBasePath -Today $today
    $latestImportSource = if ($ImportSource) { $ImportSource.ImportFile.FullName } else { "None" }

    $content = @()
    $content += "# Daily Copilot Running History"
    $content += ""
    $content += "- Date: $today"
    $content += "- Last Updated: $((Get-Date).ToString('HH:mm:ss'))"
    $content += "- Latest Import Source: $latestImportSource"
    $content += ""

    if ($ImportSource) {
        $content += "- Import Source Type: $($ImportSource.SourceType)"
        if ($ImportSource.ContainerFile) {
            $content += "- Source Archive: $($ImportSource.ContainerFile.FullName)"
        }
        if ($ImportSource.ExtractPath) {
            $content += "- Extracted To: $($ImportSource.ExtractPath)"
        }
        $content += ""
    }

    $content += "---"
    $content += ""
    $content += "## Previous Running History"
    $content += ""

    if ($previousHistory) {
        $content += Get-Content -Path $previousHistory.FullName
    }
    else {
        $content += "_No previous running history file was found._"
    }

    $content += ""
    $content += "---"
    $content += ""
    $content += "## Today's Latest Export"
    $content += ""

    if ($ImportSource) {
        $detectedVersionSource = if ($ImportSource.ContainerFile) { $ImportSource.ContainerFile.Name } else { $ImportSource.ImportFile.Name }

        $content += "- Source File: $($ImportSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
        $content += "- Last Write Time: $($ImportSource.ImportFile.LastWriteTime)"
        $content += "- File Type: $($ImportSource.ImportFile.Extension)"
        $content += "- Detected Version: $(Get-VersionNumber $detectedVersionSource)"
        $content += ""
        $content += "===== BEGIN IMPORTED EXPORT ====="
        $content += ""

        try {
            $raw = Get-Content -Path $ImportSource.ImportFile.FullName -Raw
            $content += $raw
        }
        catch {
            $content += "[ERROR] Failed to read import file: $($ImportSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
            $content += $_.Exception.Message
        }

        $content += ""
        $content += "===== END IMPORTED EXPORT ====="
    }
    else {
        $content += "_No export file for target date was found in the scan paths._"
    }

    $content += ""
    $content += "---"
    $content += ""
    $content += "## New Notes"
    $content += ""
    $content += "_Add today's notes below._"
    $content += ""

    Set-Content -Path $historyFile -Value $content -Encoding UTF8
    return $historyFile
}

function Build-ExecutiveSummaryFile {
    param(
        [datetime]$Date,
        [string]$TargetFolder,
        [string]$MasterHistoryPath,
        [object]$ImportSource
    )

    $dateString = $Date.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
    $summaryPath = Join-Path $TargetFolder "${dateString}_executive-summary.md"

    $summary = @()
    $summary += "# Executive Summary - $dateString"
    $summary += ""
    $summary += "## Source Overview"
    $summary += ""
    $summary += "- Master History: $MasterHistoryPath"

    if ($ImportSource) {
        $summary += "- Import Source Type: $($ImportSource.SourceType)"
        $summary += "- Import File: $($ImportSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
        if ($ImportSource.ContainerFile) {
            $summary += "- Archive: $($ImportSource.ContainerFile.FullName)"
        }
        if ($ImportSource.ExtractPath) {
            $summary += "- Extracted Folder: $($ImportSource.ExtractPath)"
        }
    }
    else {
        $summary += "- No import source detected for the target date."
    }

    $summary += ""
    $summary += "## Notes"
    $summary += ""
    $summary += "- This file is an operator-facing summary placeholder."
    $summary += "- Replace or expand this with a handoff summary after review."
    $summary += "- Recommended follow-up: ask Copilot to summarize the imported history into a project handoff."
    $summary += ""

    Set-Content -Path $summaryPath -Value $summary -Encoding UTF8
    return $summaryPath
}

function Split-TextFileIntoParts {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$SourceFile,

        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
        [string]$OutputRoot,

        [int]$LinesPerPart = 2000
    )

    if (-not (Test-Path $SourceFile)) {
        return $null
    }

    $baseName = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($SourceFile)
    $partsFolder = Join-Path $OutputRoot ($baseName + "_parts")

    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $partsFolder -Force | Out-Null

    Get-ChildItem -Path $partsFolder -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Name -like "${baseName}_part_*.txt" } |
        Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $partNumber = 1

    Get-Content -Path $SourceFile | ForEach-Object {
        $chunk.Add($_)

        if ($chunk.Count -ge $LinesPerPart) {
            $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
            $chunk | Set-Content -Path $partPath -Encoding UTF8
            $chunk = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
            $partNumber++
        }
    }

    if ($chunk.Count -gt 0) {
        $partPath = Join-Path $partsFolder ("{0}_part_{1:D3}.txt" -f $baseName, $partNumber)
        $chunk | Set-Content -Path $partPath -Encoding UTF8
    }

    return $partsFolder
}

function Get-MonthRecoveryFolderName {
    param([datetime]$Date)

    $monthFolder = $Date.ToString("MMM-yyyy").ToLower()

    return switch -Regex ($monthFolder) {
        '^jan-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jan', 'january' }
        '^feb-' { $monthFolder -replace '^feb', 'february' }
        '^mar-' { $monthFolder -replace '^mar', 'march' }
        '^apr-' { $monthFolder -replace '^apr', 'april' }
        '^may-' { $monthFolder -replace '^may', 'may' }
        '^jun-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jun', 'june' }
        '^jul-' { $monthFolder -replace '^jul', 'july' }
        '^aug-' { $monthFolder -replace '^aug', 'august' }
        '^sep-' { $monthFolder -replace '^sep', 'september' }
        '^oct-' { $monthFolder -replace '^oct', 'october' }
        '^nov-' { $monthFolder -replace '^nov', 'november' }
        '^dec-' { $monthFolder -replace '^dec', 'december' }
        default { $monthFolder }
    }
}

function Assert-GitRepo {
    param([string]$Path)

    if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $Path ".git"))) {
        throw "RepoPath is not a Git repository: $Path"
    }
}

# Main flow
$targetDateString = $TargetDate.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
$todayFolder = Join-Path $DailyBasePath $targetDateString
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $todayFolder -Force | Out-Null

Assert-GitRepo -Path $RepoPath

Write-Info "Scanning export files for $targetDateString"
$exports = Get-ExportFilesForDate -Paths $ScanPaths -Date $TargetDate
$latestGroup = Get-LatestExportGroup -Files $exports
$importSource = Get-BestImportSourceFromGroup -GroupFiles $latestGroup -TodayFolder $todayFolder

if ($importSource) {
    Write-Info "Selected import source: $($importSource.ImportFile.FullName)"
    Write-Info "Import type: $($importSource.SourceType)"
}
else {
    Write-Info "No import source found for $targetDateString"
}

$masterHistory = Build-MasterHistoryFile -Date $TargetDate -DailyBasePath $DailyBasePath -ImportSource $importSource
Write-Info "Built master history: $masterHistory"

$monthRecoveryFolder = Get-MonthRecoveryFolderName -Date $TargetDate
$repoSubfolder = Join-Path ("${monthRecoveryFolder}-recovery") $targetDateString
$repoTargetFolder = Join-Path $RepoPath $repoSubfolder
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $repoTargetFolder -Force | Out-Null

Copy-Item -Path $masterHistory -Destination $repoTargetFolder -Force
Write-Info "Copied master history to repo folder"

if ($importSource -and $importSource.ExtractPath -and (Test-Path $importSource.ExtractPath)) {
    $filesToCopy = Get-ChildItem -Path $importSource.ExtractPath -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object {
            -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Extension.ToLower() -in ".md", ".json", ".txt"
        }

    foreach ($file in $filesToCopy) {
        Copy-Item -Path $file.FullName -Destination $repoTargetFolder -Force
    }

    Write-Info "Copied extracted reviewable files to repo folder"
}

$summaryPath = Build-ExecutiveSummaryFile -Date $TargetDate -TargetFolder $repoTargetFolder -MasterHistoryPath $masterHistory -ImportSource $importSource
Write-Info "Built executive summary: $summaryPath"

$markdownFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $repoTargetFolder -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Extension.ToLower() -eq ".md" }

foreach ($mdFile in $markdownFiles) {
    $partsFolder = Split-TextFileIntoParts -SourceFile $mdFile.FullName -OutputRoot $repoTargetFolder -LinesPerPart $ChunkLineCount
    if ($partsFolder) {
        Write-Info "Split markdown file into parts: $partsFolder"
    }
}

if (-not $Silent) {
    Start-Process notepad.exe $masterHistory
}

if (-not $SkipGit) {
    Push-Location $RepoPath
    try {
        git checkout $BranchName
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Failed to checkout branch $BranchName" }

        git pull origin $BranchName
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Failed to pull branch $BranchName" }

        git add $repoSubfolder

        $status = git status --porcelain
        if (-not $status) {
            Write-Info "No changes to commit."
            exit 0
        }

        $commitMessage = "Add chat history files for $targetDateString"
        git commit -m $commitMessage
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Git commit failed." }

        git push origin $BranchName
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Git push failed." }

        Write-Info "Synced chat history to repo: $repoSubfolder"
    }
    finally {
        Pop-Location
    }
}
else {
    Write-Info "SkipGit specified; files prepared but not committed/pushed."
}
````

## What this fixes
- **Repo path is parameterized** instead of hardcoded.
- **Target date is parameterized**, so you can process May 20 on May 21 or later.
- It does **scan → extract → build master history → copy → split → summary placeholder → git add/commit/push** in one flow.
- It verifies that `RepoPath` exists and looks like a Git repo before trying to push. Parameter validation and script validation are standard PowerShell patterns for this kind of guardrail. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/developer/cmdlet/validating-parameter-input?view=powershell-7.5&utm_source=openai))

## Recommended usage
For a specific missed day:

```powershell
.\Sync-CopilotChatHistory.ps1 `
  -RepoPath "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History" `
  -TargetDate "2026-05-20" `
  -BranchName "upload-chat-history"
```

For today without pushing yet:

```powershell
.\Sync-CopilotChatHistory.ps1 `
  -RepoPath "E:\Co-Pilot-Chat-History" `
  -SkipGit
```

## Recommended next improvement
The weakest part still is the “executive summary” generation: right now it creates a useful placeholder, not a real AI-written summary. That’s because a local PowerShell script can’t reliably produce the kind of narrative summary you want without calling an LLM/service. So the best pattern is:
1. use this script to prepare/push the source files,
2. then ask me to summarize the new dated folder in the repo.

If you want, next I can give you a **v2** of this script that also:
- avoids copying duplicate extracted files with the same name,
- writes a log file,
- supports `-WhatIf`,
- and caps split parts by **approximate byte size** as well as line count.

## According to your original sync script
These lines control it:

```powershell
$RepoSubfolder = "${monthFolder}-recovery\$today"
$RepoTargetFolder = Join-Path $RepoPath $RepoSubfolder
```

and then:

```powershell
$markdownFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoTargetFolder -File -Filter *.md -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($mdFile in $markdownFiles) {
    Split-TextFileIntoParts -SourceFile $mdFile.FullName -OutputRoot $RepoTargetFolder -LinesPerPart $ChunkLineCount
}
```

```text
AMi project context reload:

Project structure:
- AMiDataStore = read-only legacy DOS hard-drive snapshot / reference corpus.

- It is NOT a modern .NET datastore/service repo.
- DOS GW-BASIC app = original workflow/behavior engine.
- AmiWinForms = VB.NET WinForms replacement/continuation app intended to preserve DOS workflow/look-and-feel as closely as practical.

Correct comparison framing:
- AMiDataStore = legacy storage/artifacts/source-of-truth
- DOS GW-BASIC = legacy runtime logic/workflow/menu/process behavior
- AmiWinForms = new implementation layer

Legacy DOS architecture:
- Startup is batch-driven (AUTOEXEC.BAT -> LOGIN.BAT -> GWBASIC main menu).
- MAINM/MAINMENU is the central router.
- Classic CHAIN/SHELL architecture: modules communicate through shared files, not in-memory APIs.
- Main menu routes include invoice, ledger/checks, sales, logbook, price list (PRC), boot/maintenance, phone, ENTIRE, billing/check-writing, backup, and utilities.

Legacy core accounting/data files:
- INVOICE.CHK = master invoice status/index table; key status flags include J unpaid, P paid, C corrected cert, V void, E erased.
- JOURNAL.CUR = sales journal transaction stream.
- LOGBOOK.yy = year-suffixed detailed cert/processing log.
- LEDGER.CUR = mixed debit/credit ledger stream.
- CHECK.INV = check-to-invoice linkage file.
- OTHER.CHK = non-invoice/overpayment/other checks.
- EMPNAME.DAT = sales employee/customer mapping.
- PRC\*.PRC = customer procedure price lists.
- REALNAME.DAT = abbreviated customer code to real-name mapping.
- INVOICE.NUM / MONTH.INV / LASTINVO.ICE = invoice counters/boundary tracking.
- BILL-side files include CHECKNO.DAT and multiple BILLS.* / PAYDEP.* cash-disbursement files.

Important DOS workflows:
- Create invoice -> writes JOURNAL.CUR, LOGBOOK.yy, INVOICE.CHK, INVOICE.NUM, sometimes LEDGER.CUR debit entries.
- Receive customer payment check -> reads unpaid invoices from INVOICE.CHK, marks invoice paid, appends credit to LEDGER.CUR, writes CHECK.INV linkage.
- Delete/void check receipt -> removes ledger/check-link records and resets invoice flags.
- OTHER checks are stored separately in OTHER.CHK.
- ENTIRE handles invoice-level inquiry/edit/status/report/month-boundary functions.
- BOOT handles print/update/void maintenance across multiple files.

Important DOS porting realities:
- No database; state is spread across synchronized flat files.
- Heavy cross-file consistency requirements.
- Random-access file layouts, packed numeric formats, and single-letter status semantics matter.
- 8-character uppercase customer IDs tied to PRC filenames matter.
- DOS operational behavior depends on file naming, year/month rollover conventions, and batch/runtime scripts.

AmiWinForms current state:
- Startup form is FormMainMenu.
- Main menu C opens CHECKS.
- Implemented mostly on read/report side:
  - LedgerCurReader
  - CheckInvReader
  - InvoiceChkReader
  - OtherChkReader
  - ledger view
  - company totals
  - OTHER checks view
  - find by check number
  - find by invoice number
  - doesn’t balance report
- EMPNAME editor exists and writes normalized EMPNAME.DAT.
- Sales employee wizard exists but is not fully integrated into the main transaction flow.
- FormAddChecks exists with company lookup but is not fully wired into CHECKS menu processing.

Biggest DOS vs VB gap:
- VB currently has strong legacy-file read/report parity.
- VB does NOT yet have full write/update parity for core accounting transactions.
- Missing/incomplete write-side flows include:
  - add checks to ledger/cash receipts
  - delete checks
  - add OTHER checks
  - delete OTHER checks
  - coordinated updates to LEDGER.CUR + CHECK.INV + INVOICE.CHK + OTHER.CHK

Important VB implementation notes:
- CompanyLookupService uses REALNAME.DAT and PRC-style company naming logic.
- LegacyDataPaths centralizes key legacy file locations.
- MigrationService / BackupService exist.
- DOS compatibility is explicitly preserved in several readers/forms.
- The app currently appears farther along in reading/analyzing/reporting legacy data than in reproducing legacy transactional write workflows.

High-level conclusion:
- AMiDataStore + DOS GW-BASIC together represent the legacy truth source (files + behavior).
- AmiWinForms is the replacement UI/workflow layer.
- Current modernization progress is strongest in viewing/reporting/parsing legacy files.
- The major remaining work is transactional parity: reproducing DOS write/update behavior while preserving DOS workflow and familiar look-and-feel.
```
